questions.text: A coin place below a rectangular glass block of thickness 9cm and refractive index 1.5 is viewed vertically above the block. The apparent displacement of the coin is
questions.explanation: For vertical viewing through a plane glass slab, apparent depth equals real depth divided by refractive index. With real depth 9 cm and refractive index 1.5, the apparent depth is 9 divided by 1.5 = 6 cm. The apparent displacement is the difference between real and apparent depth, which is 9 minus 6 = 3 cm. Therefore the coin appears raised by 3 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The radiator of a motor car is cooled by
questions.explanation: In a motor-car radiator, heat is carried away mainly by moving air. Although heat first conducts from the hot water to the metal tubes and fins, the standard named cooling process of the radiator itself is convection, because the moving air removes the heat from the metal surface. Radiation is comparatively less important here. Therefore the intended answer is convection.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristics of stationary waves?
options: They are formed by two identical waves travelling in opposite directions
they can be transverse or longitudinal
The distance between two successive nodes is one wavelenght
The antinode is a point of minimum displacement
questions.explanation: A stationary wave is produced by the superposition of two identical waves of the same frequency and amplitude travelling in opposite directions. That is its defining formation condition. The distance between successive nodes is half a wavelength, not one wavelength, and an antinode is where displacement is maximum, not minimum. Therefore option 0 is the correct characteristic among the choices provided.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: To produce an enlarged and erect image with a concave mirror,the object must be positioned
options: between the principal focus and the centre of the curvature
between the principal focus and the pole
questions.explanation: A concave mirror forms an erect image only when the image is virtual, and that happens when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus. In this position the image is also enlarged. If the object is at the focus, the image is at infinity, and if it is beyond the focus the image becomes real and inverted. Thus the correct position is between focus and pole.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: the property that is propagated in a traveling wave is
questions.explanation: In a travelling wave, the particles of the medium oscillate locally about their equilibrium positions, but the disturbance carries energy from one place to another. Frequency, amplitude, and wavelength are properties used to describe the wave, yet they are not themselves the quantity being transferred along the medium. Therefore the property propagated by a travelling wave is energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following eye defects can be corrected using a cylindrical lens.
questions.explanation: Astigmatism occurs when the eye does not have the same curvature in all planes, so light in different directions is focused differently. A cylindrical lens has power in one principal direction and can compensate for that unequal focusing. Myopia and presbyopia are usually corrected with spherical lenses, while chromatic aberration is a lens defect rather than an eye defect corrected this way. Therefore astigmatism is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The time rate of loss of heat by a body is proportional to the
options: difference in temprature between the body and its surroundings
ratio of the temperature of the body to that of its surroundings
questions.explanation: Newton’s law of cooling states that, for moderate temperature differences, the rate at which a body loses heat is proportional to the excess of its temperature over that of its surroundings. So the governing quantity is the temperature difference between the body and the surroundings, not either temperature taken alone and not their ratio. Hence option 0 states the correct proportionality.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If tension is maintained on a stretched string of length 0.6m, such that its fundamental frequency of 220Hz is excited, determine the velocity of the transverse wave in the string.
questions.explanation: For the fundamental mode of a stretched string fixed at both ends, the wavelength is 2L, so the frequency relation is f = v divided by 2L. Rearranging gives v = 2Lf. With L = 0.6 m and f = 220 Hz, v = 2 times 0.6 times 220 = 264 m s minus 1. Therefore the transverse wave speed in the string is 264 m s minus 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm forms a real image twice as large as the object.

the object distance is
questions.explanation: The radius of curvature is 40 cm, so the focal length of the concave mirror is 20 cm. A real image twice as large as the object has magnitude of magnification 2, so the image distance is twice the object distance. Using 1 over f = 1 over u plus 1 over v with v = 2u gives 1 over 20 = 1 over u + 1 over 2u = 3 over 2u, hence u = 30 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: water is a poor thermometric liquid because it
questions.explanation: Water is a poor thermometric liquid because it wets glass. A liquid that wets the glass tube forms an awkward meniscus and does not move cleanly in a narrow capillary, which reduces the ease and accuracy of reading. The other options are not the key reason in thermometer design. Therefore the correct thermometric defect of water among the listed choices is that it wets glass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: a ray of light which strikes a glass slab from air at normal incidence passes through the slab
options: undeviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
deviated and undisplaced at a lower speed
deviated and displaced at a lower speed
undeviated and displaced at a faster speed
questions.explanation: At normal incidence, the angle of incidence is zero, so a ray entering a glass slab does not bend at either surface. Since it continues along the same straight line, there is no angular deviation and no lateral displacement. However, light travels more slowly in glass than in air because glass is optically denser. Therefore the ray passes through undeviated and undisplaced at a lower speed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The phenomenon that makes sound persist when its source has been removed is known as
questions.explanation: Reverberation is the persistence of sound after the source has stopped, caused by repeated reflections from surrounding surfaces. The listener hears a prolonged decay rather than a separate repeated sound. Echo is a distinct delayed reflection, while rarefaction is the low-pressure region of a sound wave. Therefore the phenomenon described is reverberation, which corresponds to option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: the pressure of 3 moles of an ideal gas at a temperature of 27°C having a volume of 10-3m3 is
questions.explanation: Apply the ideal gas law, P = nRT divided by V. Convert 27 degrees C to 300 K. With n = 3 mol, R = 8.31 J mol^-1 K^-1, and V = 1.0 x 10^-3 m^3, P = 3 x 8.31 x 300 divided by 10^-3 = 7.479 x 10^6 Pa. The options are poorly formatted, but the intended match is 7.47 x 10^6 N m^-2, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Vibration in a stretched spring cannot be polarized because they are
questions.explanation: Polarization is possible only for transverse waves because their vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation and can be restricted to one plane. In a stretched spring, the vibration referred to here is longitudinal, meaning particle motion is along the direction of travel. Longitudinal waves cannot be polarized. Therefore the correct option is 2, longitudinal waves.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows the velocity-time graph of a vehicle. Its acceleration and retardation respectively are
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the slope of the velocity-time graph. From 0 to 20 s, velocity rises from 0 to 80 m s^-1, so acceleration = 80 divided by 20 = 4.0 m s^-2. Retardation is the magnitude of the negative slope from 50 to 90 s, where velocity falls from 80 to 0 in 40 s, giving 80 divided by 40 = 2.0 m s^-2. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The figure above represents a frictionless pulley system in which a weight W is in equilibrium with a weight of 40N. Find the value of W
questions.explanation: In a frictionless pulley, the tension is the same throughout the rope. The 40 N load is attached to a movable pulley supported by two upward rope segments, so 2T = 40 N and T = 20 N. The weight W hangs from the free end of the same rope, therefore W = T = 20 N. So the correct answer is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows a solid figure with base PQ and center of gravity G on a inclined plane. Which of the following statements is correct
options: The solid will fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid will fall over if the vertical line through lies inside the base
The solid will not fall over if the vertical line through G lies outside the base
The solid can never fall over
questions.explanation: A body remains stable so long as the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base of support. If that line falls outside the base PQ, the turning effect of the weight makes the object topple. The diagram is a standard stability case on an inclined plane. Therefore option 0 states the correct condition for falling over.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows a lift pump with valves at P and Q. During a downward stroke of the piston
options: P is open while Q is closed
P is closed while Q is open
questions.explanation: In a lift pump, Q is the lower inlet valve and P is the valve in the piston. During the downward stroke, the piston pushes water below it and increases pressure there, so valve Q closes. At the same time, water above the piston passes through the piston because valve P opens. Therefore P is open while Q is closed, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the J-tube above, Y and X are on the same horizontal level and 30cm3 of air is trapped above Y when the atmospheric pressure is 75cm Hg, calculate the volume of air trapped above Y when 15cm Hg is now poured into the limb above X
questions.explanation: Initially, Y and X are at the same level, so the trapped air has atmospheric pressure, 75 cm Hg, and volume 30 cm^3. When 15 cm Hg is poured into the other limb, the trapped air pressure becomes 75 + 15 = 90 cm Hg. With temperature constant, Boyle's law gives P1V1 = P2V2. Thus V2 = 75 x 30 divided by 90 = 25 cm^3. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above represents a transverse electromagnetic wave travelling with speed 3.0 x 108ms-1. What is the frequency of the wave.
questions.explanation: From the wave sketch, the 0.3 m length contains three complete wavelengths, so wavelength lambda = 0.3 divided by 3 = 0.1 m. Using v = f lambda with v = 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 gives f = 3.0 x 10^8 divided by 0.1 = 3.0 x 10^9 Hz. Therefore the correct option is 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows the prism arrangement in a
questions.explanation: The arrangement uses two right-angled prisms to turn the light path through 90 degrees twice. That lets an observer see over or around an obstruction without moving the line of sight directly. This is the standard prism arrangement of a periscope, not a spectrometer, projector, or full binocular optical system. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the circuit above, the ammeter reads a current of 5.0 A when R = 8Ω and reads 7.0A when R = 5Ω. The value of the unknown resistance X is
questions.explanation: The resistors are in series, so I = E divided by R + X. When R = 8 ohms and I = 5 A, E = 5(8 + X) = 40 + 5X. When R = 5 ohms and I = 7 A, E = 7(5 + X) = 35 + 7X. Equating the two expressions gives 40 + 5X = 35 + 7X, so X = 2.5 ohms. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the circuit above, The potential across each capacitor is 100V. The total energy stored in the two capacitors is
questions.explanation: The two capacitors are connected in parallel, so each has the same potential difference, 100 V. Total energy stored is the sum of the individual energies: U = 1/2 C1V^2 + 1/2 C2V^2 = 1/2 (2 + 3) x 10^-6 x 100^2. This gives 1/2 x 5 x 10^-6 x 10^4 = 2.5 x 10^-2 J. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, if the internal resistance of the cell is zero, the ration of the powers P1 and P2 dissipated by R1 and R2
questions.explanation: The resistors are in parallel across an ideal cell, so each resistor has the same voltage across it. Power in a resistor is P = V^2 divided by R. Therefore P1 = V^2 divided by R1 and P2 = V^2 divided by R2. Taking the ratio gives P1/P2 = R2/R1. Hence option 0 is the correct expression.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the series a.c circuit shown above, the p.d across the inductor is 8Vr.m.s and that across the resistor is 6Vr.m.s. The effective voltage is
questions.explanation: In a series a.c. circuit containing resistance and inductance, the voltage across the resistor is in phase with current while the voltage across the inductor leads by 90 degrees. So the supply voltage is the phasor sum, not the arithmetic sum. Thus V = square root of 6^2 + 8^2 = square root of 100 = 10 V. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
The velocity y of a particle in a time t is given by the equation

y = 10 + 2t\(^2\)

Find the instantaneous acceleration after 5 seconds
questions.explanation: The velocity is v = 10 + 2t^2. Instantaneous acceleration is a = dv/dt, so differentiate to get a = 4t. At t = 5 s, a = 4 x 5 = 20 m s^-2. The constant term 10 contributes nothing to acceleration. Therefore the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A simple pendulum has a period of 17.0s. When the length is shorten by 1.5m, its period is 8.5s. Calculate the original length of the pendulum
questions.explanation: For a simple pendulum, T = 2pi square root of L/g, so T^2 is proportional to L. Let the original length be L. Then 17.0^2 divided by 8.5^2 equals L divided by L - 1.5. Since 17.0 divided by 8.5 is 2, the squared ratio is 4. So 4 = L/(L - 1.5), giving 4L - 6 = L, hence L = 2.0 m. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A sonometer wire is vibrating at frequency fo. If the tension in the wire is doubled while the length and the mass per unit length are kept constant, the new frequency of vibration is
questions.explanation: For a vibrating string, f = (1/2L) square root of T divided by mu. Since the length L and mass per unit length mu are constant, frequency is proportional to square root of tension. Doubling the tension multiplies the frequency by square root of 2. Therefore the new frequency is fo square root of 2, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A travelling wave moving from left to right has an amplitude of 0.15m, a frequency of 550Hz and a wavelength of 0.01m. The equation describing the wave is
questions.explanation: A progressive wave travelling to the right can be written as y = A sin 2pi(x/lambda - ft). Here A = 0.15 m, lambda = 0.01 m, and f = 550 Hz. Since 2pi/lambda = 200pi and f lambda = 5.5, the equation becomes y = 0.15 sin 200pi(x - 5.5t). This matches option 0 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A transverse wave is applied to a string whose mass per unit length is 3 x 10-2kgm-1. If the string is under a tension 12N, the speed of the propagation of the wave is
questions.explanation: Wave speed on a stretched string is v = square root of T divided by mu. With T = 12 N and mu = 3 x 10^-2 kg m^-1, v = square root of 12 divided by 0.03 = square root of 400 = 20 m s^-1. Therefore option 1 is correct. The unit check is consistent because N over kg m^-1 reduces to m^2 s^-2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An engineer intends to deviate a light ray from its path by 120o through reflection from a plane mirror. Calculate the angle of incidence
questions.explanation: The attached diagram shows deviation as the angle between the reflected ray and the straight continuation of the incident ray beyond the mirror. For reflection at a plane mirror, that deviation is d = 180 degrees minus 2i, where i is the angle of incidence. Substituting d = 120 degrees gives 120 = 180 - 2i, so 2i = 60 and i = 30 degrees. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows a maximum and minimum thermometer divided into three portions P, Q and R. Which of the following is true about the respective content of P,Q and R
questions.explanation: A maximum-minimum thermometer of Six's type contains alcohol in the upper bulb and stem regions and mercury in the lower U-shaped bend. From the diagram, P is in the upper left liquid region, Q is the lower bend, and R is the upper right region. Therefore P, Q, and R contain alcohol, mercury, and alcohol respectively. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows two capacitors P and Q of capacitance 5μF and 10μF. Find the charges stored in P and Q respectively
questions.explanation: The two capacitors are connected in parallel across the 20 V source, so each capacitor has 20 V across it. Charge is given by Q = CV. For capacitor P, Q = 5 microfarads x 20 V = 100 microcoulombs. For capacitor Q, Q = 10 microfarads x 20 V = 200 microcoulombs. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, the values of V1 and V2 are respectively
questions.explanation: The cell has emf 2 V and internal resistance 1 ohm, in series with external resistors 3 ohms and 2 ohms. Total resistance is 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ohms, so current I = 2/6 = 1/3 A. Therefore V1 across 3 ohms is I x 3 = 1 V, and V2 across 2 ohms is I x 2 = 2/3 V. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The correct position for a fuse in the diagram above is
questions.explanation: A fuse must be placed in the live wire so that if it melts, the appliance is disconnected from the dangerous supply line. In the diagram, P is on the live lead, Q is on the neutral lead, and S is on the earth lead. Therefore the correct position for the fuse is P, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the a.c circuit above, the current value is
questions.explanation: This is a series R-C a.c. circuit with resistance 30 ohms and capacitive reactance 40 ohms supplied at 200 V rms. The impedance is Z = square root of 30^2 + 40^2 = 50 ohms. Hence the current is I = V/Z = 200/50 = 4.00 A. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, which of the simple pendula will resonate with P when set into oscillation
questions.explanation: Simple pendulums resonate when they have the same natural frequency, which for small oscillations means the same length because T = 2pi square root of L/g. From the diagram, pendulum T has the same length as P, whereas Q, R, S, and U are visibly different. Therefore T will resonate with P. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If ray travelling in air is incident on a transparent medium as shown in the diagram, the refractive index of the medium is given as
questions.explanation: By Snell's law, refractive index n = sin i divided by sin r, with angles measured from the normal. In the figure, alpha is drawn between the incident ray and the surface, so i = 90 degrees minus alpha and sin i = cos alpha. Beta is the refracted angle with the normal. Therefore n = cos alpha divided by sin beta, which is option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above , the current I is
questions.explanation: The 10 ohm and 5 ohm resistors form a parallel combination with equivalent resistance 10 x 5 divided by 10 + 5 = 10/3 ohms. This is in series with 3 ohms and 1 ohm, giving total resistance 3 + 1 + 10/3 = 22/3 ohms. Therefore I = V/R = 6 divided by 22/3 = 18/22 = 9/11 A. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows two capacitors P and Q of capacitance 2μF and 4μF respectively connected to a d.c source. The ratio of energy stored in P to Q is
questions.explanation: Capacitors P and Q are connected in parallel, so the same voltage acts across both. Energy stored in a capacitor is U = 1/2 CV^2. Since V is common, the ratio of energies equals the ratio of capacitances: UP:UQ = 2 microfarads : 4 microfarads = 1:2. Hence the correct option is 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows the capacitors C\(_1\), C\(_2\) and C\(_3\) 2μF, 6μF and 3μF respectively. The potential difference across C\(_1\), C\(_2\) and C\(_3\) respectively are
questions.explanation: The three capacitors are in series across 12 V, so each carries the same charge. First find the equivalent capacitance: 1/Ceq = 1/2 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 1, so Ceq = 1 microfarad. Charge Q = CeqV = 1 microfarad x 12 V = 12 microcoulombs. Hence V1 = 12/2 = 6 V, V2 = 12/6 = 2 V, and V3 = 12/3 = 4 V. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows a closed side 0.5m in a uniform electric field E in the direction shown by the arrows. What is the flux Φ for the box?
questions.explanation: For any closed surface in a uniform electric field with no charge enclosed, the net electric flux is zero. The amount of flux entering the box equals the amount leaving it, so the algebraic sum cancels. This follows directly from Gauss's law. The side length of 0.5 m does not affect the net result. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the circuit diagram above , the ammeter reads a current of 3A when R is 5Ω and 6A when R is 2Ω. Determine the value of x
questions.explanation: The two resistors are in parallel across the same cell, so total current I = E(1/R + 1/x). When R = 5 ohms, 3 = E(1/5 + 1/x). When R = 2 ohms, 6 = E(1/2 + 1/x). Solving these simultaneous equations gives x = 8 ohms. Therefore the correct option is 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, determine the r.m.s current
questions.explanation: Treat the circuit as a series resistor and inductor with R = 4 ohms and inductive reactance Xl = 3 ohms, read from the diagram. The impedance is Z = sqrt(R squared + Xl squared) = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5 ohms. Hence the r.m.s current is I = V/Z = 240/5 = 48 A. This matches option 1 and is physically consistent for a 240 V a.c. source.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above show s the force-extension curve of a piece of wire. The energy stored when the wire is stretched from E to F is?
questions.explanation: The energy stored between E and F equals the area under the force-extension graph over that interval. At E = 0.05 m, force is 0.1 N; at F = 0.10 m, force is 0.2 N. The area is a trapezium: 1/2 x (0.1 + 0.2) x (0.10 - 0.05) = 0.5 x 0.3 x 0.05 = 7.5 x 10^-3 J. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The diagram above shows the force (F) acting on an object through a distance (x). The work done on this object is expressed as
questions.explanation: Work done by a variable force is the area under the force-distance graph. The graph rises linearly from zero to force F at distance x, so the area is a triangle. Therefore work W = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x x x F = Fx/2 joules. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: From the diagram above, determine the value of the resistance X
questions.explanation: The 2 ohm resistor, the parallel section, and the 1.5 ohm resistor are in series across 12 V. Since the current is 2 A, the total resistance is 12/2 = 6 ohms. So the parallel middle section must be 6 - 2 - 1.5 = 2.5 ohms. For 3 ohms in parallel with X, 3X divided by 3 + X = 2.5, giving X = 15 ohms. Hence option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance 10μF carrying a charge of 100μC
questions.explanation: Use the capacitor energy formula U = Q^2 divided by 2C. Here Q = 100 microcoulombs = 1.0 x 10^-4 C and C = 10 microfarads = 1.0 x 10^-5 F. So U = (1.0 x 10^-4)^2 divided by 2 x 1.0 x 10^-5 = 1.0 x 10^-8 divided by 2.0 x 10^-5 = 5 x 10^-4 J. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When connected to a mains of 250V, the fuse rating in the plug of an electric device of 1 KW is
questions.explanation: The operating current of the device is I = P/V = 1000/250 = 4 A. A fuse should be rated slightly above the normal operating current so it does not blow during proper use but still provides protection. Among the options, the nearest suitable rating above 4 A is 5 A. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The eye controls the amount of light reaching the retina by adjusting the
questions.explanation: The iris controls the amount of light reaching the retina by varying the size of the pupil. In bright light it constricts the pupil, and in dim light it enlarges it. The cornea mainly refracts light, the retina receives the image, and the optic nerve carries impulses to the brain. Therefore the correct option is 1, iris.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric iron is rated 1000W, 230V. What is the resistance of its elements?
questions.explanation: An electric iron is essentially resistive, so its rating satisfies P = V squared over R. Rearranging gives R = V squared divided by P. Using V = 230 V and P = 1000 W, R = 230 × 230 divided by 1000 = 52900 divided by 1000 = 52.9 ohms. This corresponds exactly to option 1, so that is the defensible final answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electric field between two - point charges is shown in the diagram above. What types of charges are at X and Y?
options: Both X and Y are negative
Both X and Y are positive
X is positive and Y is negative
X is negative and Y is positive
questions.explanation: Electric field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges. In the diagram, the arrows are directed outward from both X and Y, showing that each point charge is a source of field lines. Therefore both X and Y are positive. Hence the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electromagnetic wave that can produce a heating effect on the environment is
questions.explanation: Infrared radiation is the part of the electromagnetic spectrum most directly associated with heating. Bodies at ordinary temperatures emit strongly in the infrared, and absorption of infrared raises temperature. Ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays are more associated with ionization or photochemical effects than ordinary environmental heating. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: an electric cell with nominal voltage E has a resistance of 3Ω connected across it. If the voltage falls to 0.6E, the internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation: The terminal p.d. across the 3 ohm resistor is 0.6E, so the current is I = 0.6E divided by 3 = 0.2E. For a cell of emf E and internal resistance r, E = I(R + r). Substituting gives E = 0.2E(3 + r). Dividing by 0.2E gives 5 = 3 + r, so r = 2 ohms. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
\(^{23}_{11}\)Na + X → \(^{20}_9\)F + \(^4_2\)He

What particle is X in the reaction above?
questions.explanation: Conserve nucleon number and charge in the nuclear equation. For mass numbers, 23 + A = 20 + 4, so A = 1. For atomic numbers, 11 + Z = 9 + 2, so Z = 0. The particle with mass number 1 and charge 0 is a neutron. Therefore option 2 is the intended answer, even though the option text incorrectly says neurons instead of neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Pure silicon can be converted to a p-type by adding a controlled amount of
questions.explanation: P-type silicon is produced by doping pure tetravalent silicon with trivalent impurity atoms such as boron or indium. Each impurity forms only three covalent bonds, leaving one bond incomplete and creating a hole. Holes then become the majority charge carriers. Pentavalent doping would instead supply extra electrons and produce n-type material. Therefore the correct choice is trivalent atoms.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
The energy associated with the photon of a radio transmission at 3 x 105 Hz is

[h = 6.63 x 10-34Js]
questions.explanation: The energy of a photon is given by E = hf. Using h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s and f = 3 x 10^5 Hz, E = 6.63 x 10^-34 x 3 x 10^5 = 19.89 x 10^-29 J = 1.989 x 10^-28 J. Rounded appropriately, this is 2.00 x 10^-28 J. The units and power of ten are consistent with option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The percentage of the original nuclei of the sample of a radioactive substance left after 5 half - lives is
questions.explanation: After n half-lives, the fraction of radioactive nuclei remaining is (1/2)^n. For 5 half-lives, the fraction left is (1/2)^5 = 1/32 = 0.03125. Converting to a percentage gives 3.125 percent. The nearest option is 3 percent. So about 3 percent of the original nuclei remains after five half-lives, making option 2 the defensible answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: From the generating station to each substation power is transmitted at a very high voltage so as to reduce
questions.explanation: Electrical power transmitted is P = VI. For a fixed power, increasing the transmission voltage reduces the current. Since resistive heating loss in conductors is I^2R, a smaller current greatly reduces the heat produced in the transmission system. Hysteresis and eddy-current losses are associated mainly with magnetic materials, not the transmission lines. Hence the purpose of very high voltage transmission is to reduce heating losses.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The particle that is responsible for the nuclear fission in a nuclear reactor is
questions.explanation: In a nuclear reactor, fission is commonly initiated when a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 absorbs a neutron. The absorbed neutron makes the nucleus unstable, causing it to split and release energy together with more neutrons. These emitted neutrons sustain the chain reaction. Protons and electrons are not the usual initiating particles in reactor fission. Therefore the responsible particle is the neutron.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A transistor is used in the amplification of signals because it
questions.explanation: A transistor amplifies because a small input signal controls a larger current through the device. In practice, a small change at the base-emitter junction produces a much larger change in collector current, allowing signal gain. Simply having electrons and holes present is not enough to explain amplification, and high power consumption is irrelevant. Therefore the correct statement is that it controls the flow of current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The carbon-granules microphone works on the principle of change in
questions.explanation: A carbon-granule microphone operates because sound waves compress and relax the carbon granules. That changes the contact resistance between the granules. When a steady voltage source is connected, the varying resistance causes the current to vary in step with the sound, producing an electrical signal. The operating principle is therefore change in resistance, not inductance, capacitance, or voltage directly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At what frequency would a capacitor of 2.5μF used in the radio circuit have a reactance of 250Ω
questions.explanation: For a capacitor, reactance is Xc = 1 divided by 2πfC. Rearranging gives f = 1 divided by 2πXcC. Substituting Xc = 250 ohms and C = 2.5 x 10^-6 F gives f = 1 divided by 2π x 250 x 2.5 x 10^-6 = 800 divided by π hertz. This matches option 1 exactly, with correct units and algebra.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A current of 0.5 A flowing 3h Deposits 2g of metal during electrolysis. The quantity of the same metal that would be deposited by the currents of 1.5A flowing in 1h is
questions.explanation: For the same metal, mass deposited during electrolysis is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed, so m is proportional to It. In the first case, 0.5 x 3 = 1.5 ampere-hours gives 2 g. In the second case, 1.5 x 1 = 1.5 ampere-hours as well. Since the charge passed is the same, the deposited mass is the same. Therefore the correct answer is 2 g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true of the properties of a moving coil galvanometer?
options: THe coil has a small area
There are strong hair springs to gives a large control panlel
There is a strong permanent magnet to give high magnetic flux
it has a small number of turns of coil
questions.explanation: A moving-coil galvanometer is designed for high sensitivity, so the deflecting torque must be large even for small currents. Since torque is proportional to NBAI, one key design feature is a strong permanent magnet that provides a large magnetic flux density. Small coil area, few turns, or strong control springs would all reduce sensitivity. Hence the true statement is that it has a strong permanent magnet.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A bead travelling on a straight line wire is brought to rest at 0.2 by friction. If the mass of the bead is 0.01kg and the coefficient of friction between the bead and the wire is 0.1, determine the work done by the friction

[g = 10ms\(^2\)]
questions.explanation: The frictional force on the bead is F = μN = μmg. Using μ = 0.1, m = 0.01 kg, and g = 10 m s^-2 gives F = 0.1 x 0.01 x 10 = 0.01 N. If the bead comes to rest after moving 0.2 m, the work done by friction is W = Fd = 0.01 x 0.2 = 0.002 J = 2 x 10^-3 J. So option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: On top of a spiral spring of the force constant 500Nm-1 is placed a mass of 5 x 10-3 kg. If the spring is compressed downwards by a length of 0.02m and then released, calculate the height to which the mass is projected
questions.explanation: The compressed spring stores elastic potential energy equal to 1/2 kx^2. On release, this becomes gravitational potential energy mgh at the highest point. With k = 500 N m^-1 and x = 0.02 m, the stored energy is 1/2 x 500 x 0.02^2 = 0.1 J. Setting 0.1 = 0.005 x 10 x h gives h = 2 m. Therefore the mass rises to a height of 2 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A test tube of radius 1.0cm is loaded to 8.8g. If is placed upright in water, find the depth to which it would sink
questions.explanation: For upright floating equilibrium, the tube displaces its own weight of water. In water, 8.8 g corresponds to 8.8 cm^3 displaced because the density is 1 g per cm^3. The cross-sectional area is pi r^2 = pi times 1.0^2 = pi cm^2. Hence depth immersed = displaced volume divided by area = 8.8 over pi, about 2.8 cm. This matches option 0 and is physically reasonable.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A hose of cross-sectional area 0.5m2 is used to discharge water from a water tanker at a velocity of 60ms-1 in 20s into a container. If the container is filled completely, the volume of the container is
questions.explanation: The volume delivered by the hose is volume flow rate multiplied by time. Since flow rate is area times speed, V = Avt. Using A = 0.5 m^2, v = 60 m s^-1, and t = 20 s gives V = 0.5 x 60 x 20 = 600 m^3. The dimensions reduce correctly to cubic metres. Hence the volume of the container is 600 m^3, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If an object just begins to slide on a surface inclined at 30o to the horizontal,the coefficient of friction is
questions.explanation: At the instant an object is just about to slide on an inclined plane, limiting friction acts and the coefficient of friction satisfies μ = tan θ. Here the plane is inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal, so μ = tan 30 degrees = 1 divided by root 3. This follows from resolving the weight into parallel and normal components. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Water does not drop through an open umbrella of silk materials unless the inside of the umbrella is touched. This is due to
questions.explanation: Water does not readily pass through the tiny openings in the silk because surface tension forms a stretched film across the pores. That film resists breaking and so prevents dripping. When the inside is touched, the film is disturbed or broken and water can then pass through. Osmotic pressure and viscosity do not explain this effect. Therefore the correct answer is surface tension.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The stylus of a phonograph record exerts a force of 7.7 x 10\(^{-2}\)N on a groove of radius 10\(^{-5}\)m. Compute the pressure exerted by the stylus on the groove
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. Taking the contact area as circular, A = πr^2 = π x 10^-10 m^2 because r = 10^-5 m. Then P = 7.7 x 10^-2 divided by π x 10^-10, which is about 2.45 x 10^8 N m^-2. The scientific notation, units, and arithmetic are consistent. Hence option 0 is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A piece of stone attached to one end of a string is whirled round in a horizontal circle and the string suddenly cuts. The stone will fly off in a direction
options: towards the center of the circle
questions.explanation: While the stone moves in a circle, the string supplies the centripetal force but does not determine the direction of the instantaneous velocity. At every point, the velocity is tangential to the path. When the string breaks, the centripetal force disappears and the stone continues in the direction it was moving at that instant. The attached diagram is consistent with this. So the stone flies off tangentially.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 90cm uniform lever has a load of 30N suspended at 15cm from one of its ends. If the fulcrum is at the center of gravity, the force that must be applied at its other end to keep it in horizontal equilibrium is
questions.explanation: The fulcrum is at the centre of gravity of the 90 cm uniform lever, so it is 45 cm from either end. The 30 N load is 15 cm from one end, so it is 45 minus 15 = 30 cm from the fulcrum. Taking moments about the fulcrum, 30 x 30 = F x 45. Solving gives F = 20 N. The image agrees with this geometry, so option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A satellite is in a parking orbit if its period is
options: less than the period of the earth
more than the period of the earth
equal to the period of the earth
the square of the period of the earth
questions.explanation: A satellite is in a parking orbit here in the sense of remaining over the same part of the Earth, which requires an orbital period equal to Earth’s rotational period. If its period were shorter or longer, it would drift relative to the Earth’s surface. Thus the necessary condition is that its period matches that of the Earth. Therefore the correct option is equal to the period of the Earth.

The table above shows the saturation vapour pressure against temperature in a certain town. If the vapour pressure in this town at 20oC is 10mmHg, what is the relative humidity?
questions.explanation: Relative humidity is the actual vapour pressure divided by the saturation vapour pressure at the same temperature, multiplied by 100 percent. At 20 degrees Celsius, the table gives saturation vapour pressure as 17.50 mmHg, while the actual vapour pressure is 10 mmHg. Therefore relative humidity = 10 divided by 17.50 x 100 = 57.14 percent, approximately 57.0 percent. That matches option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A turning fork of frequency 340Hz is vibrated just above a cylindrical tube of height 1.2m. If water is slowly poured into the tube, at what maximum height will resonance occur.

[speed of sound in air = 340ms-1]
questions.explanation: A tube with water rising inside behaves as a closed pipe, so the first resonance occurs when the air-column length is one quarter of a wavelength. Since v = 340 m s^-1 and f = 340 Hz, the wavelength is 1.0 m. Hence resonant air-column length is 0.25 m. The tube is 1.2 m tall, so the water height then is 1.2 minus 0.25 = 0.95 m. The diagram supports this.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: By what factor will the size of an object placed 10cm from a convex lens be increased if the image is seen on a screen placed 25cm from the lens?
questions.explanation: Linear magnification for a lens is the image distance divided by the object distance in magnitude. The object is 10 cm from the lens and the image is formed on a screen 25 cm from the lens, so magnification = 25 divided by 10 = 2.5. Since the question asks by what factor the size is increased, the correct value is 2.5. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Thermal equilibrium between two object exist when
options: the temperature of both objects are equal
the quantity of heat of both objects is the same
the heat capacities of both objects are the same
one object losses heat continuously to the other
questions.explanation: Two objects are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same temperature, so there is no net heat flow between them. This is the content of the zeroth law of thermodynamics. Equal heat content is not required, because that depends on mass and material, and equal heat capacity is also unnecessary. Therefore the correct condition is simply equality of temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An open pipe closed at one end produces its first fundamental note. If the velocity of sound in air is P and t the length of the pipe, the frequency of the note is
questions.explanation: A pipe that is open at one end and closed at the other has its fundamental mode when the closed end is a displacement node and the open end is an antinode. In that mode, the pipe length equals one quarter of the wavelength. If the pipe length is t, then λ = 4t. Using f = v divided by λ gives f = v divided by 4t. So option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
On a fairly cool rainy day when the temperature is 20oC, the length of a steel railroad track is 20m. What will be its length on a hot a dry day when the temperature is 40oC?

[coefficient of linear expansion of steel = 11 x 10-6K-1]
questions.explanation: Linear expansion is given by ΔL = αLΔT. Here α = 11 x 10^-6 K^-1, L = 20 m, and the temperature rise is 40 minus 20 = 20 K. So ΔL = 11 x 10^-6 x 20 x 20 = 4.4 x 10^-3 m. The new length is 20 + 0.0044 = 20.0044 m, which rounds to 20.004 m. Therefore option 2 is the best match.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If an object is placed between two parallel plane mirrors with their reflecting surfaces facing each other, how many images of the object will be formed?
questions.explanation: With two parallel plane mirrors facing each other, light reflected in one mirror is reflected again in the other, and this process repeats continuously. Each image acts as an object for further image formation, producing an endless succession in the ideal case. Therefore the number of images is infinite. Finite answers such as two, four, or eight would apply only to other mirror arrangements or non-ideal restrictions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The phenomenon where by the water droplets in the atmosphere combines with dust particles in the air to reduce visibility is
questions.explanation: Fog consists of tiny water droplets suspended close to the ground, often formed around dust or smoke particles that act as condensation nuclei. These droplets scatter light strongly and reduce visibility. Cloud is the broader atmospheric term and usually refers to higher altitude masses, while hail consists of ice. Mist is generally thinner and less visibility-reducing than fog. Therefore the correct answer is fog.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At what position will an object be placed in front of a concave mirror in order to obtain an image at infinity?
options: At the pole of the mirror
at the center of the curvature
Between the principal focus and the center of curvature
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, if an object is placed at the principal focus, rays reflected from the mirror emerge parallel to the principal axis. Parallel reflected rays correspond to an image formed at infinity. At the pole or centre of curvature the image is formed at finite distance instead. Therefore the object must be at the principal focus to produce an image at infinity, making option 1 correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 2000W electric heater is used to heat a metal object of mass 5kg initially at 10oC. If a temperature rise of 30oC is obtained after 10min, the heat capacity of the material is
questions.explanation: The heater delivers energy Q = Pt = 2000 x 600 = 1.2 x 10^6 J in 10 minutes. Heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of the whole object by 1 degree, so C = Q divided by the temperature rise = 1.2 x 10^6 divided by 30 = 4.0 x 10^4 J per degree Celsius. The 5 kg mass is irrelevant because specific heat capacity was not asked.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
If 1.2 x 10^6J of heat energy is given off in 1 sec from a vessel maintained at a temperature gradient of 30Km-1, the surface area of the vessel is

[ thermal conductivity of the vessel = 400Wm-1K-1]
questions.explanation: Heat conducted per second is given by P = kA multiplied by the temperature gradient. The vessel gives off 1.2 x 10^6 J in 1 s, so P = 1.2 x 10^6 W. With k = 400 W m^-1 K^-1 and gradient = 30 K m^-1, A = P divided by k times gradient = 1.2 x 10^6 divided by 400 x 30 = 100 m^2. That is 1.0 x 10^2 m^2, option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A positive charged rod X is brought near as uncharged metal sphere Y and is then touched by a finger with X still in place. When the finger is removed, the result is that y has
options: no charge and a zero potential
a positive charge and zero potential
a negative charge and positive potential
a negative charge and a negative potential
questions.explanation: A positively charged rod near an uncharged metal sphere attracts electrons toward the near side and leaves the far side relatively positive. When the sphere is touched to earth while the rod remains in place, electrons flow from earth into the sphere. Removing the finger first traps the excess electrons. After the rod is removed, the sphere remains negatively charged and therefore at a negative potential. So option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, if each of the resistors can dissipate a maximum of 18W without becoming excessively heated, what is the maximum power the circuit can dissipate?
questions.explanation: The two 2 ohm resistors inside the rectangular branch are in parallel, so their equivalent resistance is 1 ohm. This is in series with the outer 2 ohm resistor, giving total resistance 3 ohms. If total current is I, the series resistor dissipates 2I^2 watts, while each parallel resistor dissipates I^2 divided by 2 watts. The series resistor reaches 18 W first, giving I^2 = 9. Total circuit power is then I^2R = 9 x 3 = 27 W.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: I the diagram above, what would happen to the current I, if another resistor, R2, is connected in parallel to R1?
options: It will increase because the equivalent resistance will increase
It will decrease if R2 is greater than R1
It will increase because the effective resistance will decrease
It will decrease if R2 is less than R1
questions.explanation: Connecting another resistor in parallel with R1 reduces the equivalent resistance because the reciprocal resistances add. Therefore the effective resistance of the circuit becomes smaller than R1 alone. With the supply voltage unchanged, Ohm’s law gives total current I = V divided by the equivalent resistance, so the current drawn from the source increases. The diagram is consistent with a single supply feeding the resistor network. Thus option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wire of 5Ω resistance is drawn out so that its new length is two times the original length. If the resistivity of the wire remains the same and the cross-sectional area is halved, the new resistance is
questions.explanation: Resistance is R = ρL divided by A. The new wire has twice the original length and half the original cross-sectional area, while resistivity stays the same. Therefore the new resistance is R' = ρ x 2L divided by A over 2 = 4ρL divided by A = 4R. Starting from 5 ohms, the new resistance is 4 x 5 = 20 ohms. So option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electron of charge 1.6 x 10-19C is accelerated between two metal plates. If the kinetics energy of the electron is 4.8 x 10-17J, the potential difference between the plate is
questions.explanation: An electron accelerated through a potential difference V gains kinetic energy equal to qV. Hence V = KE divided by q. Using KE = 4.8 x 10^-17 J and q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C gives V = 4.8 divided by 1.6 x 10^2 = 3.0 x 10^2 V = 300 V. The power of ten and units are correct, so option 2 is the right answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A magnetic field is said to exist at a point if a force is
options: exerted on a stationary charge at the point
exerted on a moving charge at the point
questions.explanation: A magnetic field is detected by the force it exerts on a moving charge. The magnetic force is F = qvB sin theta, so if the charge is stationary, v = 0 and no magnetic force acts. That is why a stationary charge cannot be used in this definition. Therefore the correct statement is that a force is exerted on a moving charge at the point. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of light rays show the widest separation in the spectrum of white light
questions.explanation: The visible spectrum is ordered red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet. The widest separation among the listed pairs must therefore come from the pair that are farthest apart in this order. Violet and red would be widest overall, but that pair is not offered. Of the given options, blue and red are farthest separated. The attached spectrum sketch is consistent with that ordering. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The most suitable cell used for short interval switches in electric bells is a
questions.explanation: A Leclanche cell is suitable for devices like electric bells that operate intermittently for short intervals. It can supply current in brief bursts and recover during the intervals between use. Storage cells such as lead-acid or nickel-iron are not the standard textbook answer here, and the Daniell cell is not well suited to that application. Therefore the most suitable cell is the Leclanche cell, option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A ray incident on a glass prism undergoes minimum deviation when the
options: incident angle is equal to the angle of refraction
incident angle is equal to the angle of emergence
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation through a prism, the light path inside the prism is symmetric. This means the angle of incidence equals the angle of emergence, and the two internal angles of refraction are also equal. That is the standard condition used in prism optics. An incident angle equal to the refracted angle is not the defining condition. Therefore the correct option is that the incident angle equals the angle of emergence.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The count rate of a radioactive material is 800 count/min. If the half-life of the material is 4 days, what would the count rate be in 16 days later
questions.explanation: The count rate halves every half-life. Here the half-life is 4 days, and 16 days correspond to 16 divided by 4 = 4 half-lives. Therefore the new count rate is 800 x 1 over 2 to the power 4 = 800 divided by 16 = 50 counts per minute. The decay reasoning and arithmetic are straightforward. Thus option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A circuit has an area of 0.4m2 and consists of 50 loops of wire. If the loops are twisted and allowed to rotate at a constant angular velocity of 10 rad s-1 in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4T, the amplitude of the induced voltage is
questions.explanation: For a rotating coil in a magnetic field, the maximum induced emf is E0 = NBAω. Substituting N = 50, B = 0.4 T, A = 0.4 m^2, and ω = 10 rad s^-1 gives E0 = 50 x 0.4 x 0.4 x 10 = 80 V. Since the question asks for amplitude, the peak value is required, not an rms value. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The force on a charge moving with velocity v in a magnetic field B is half of the maximum force when the angle between v and B is
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge is F = qvB sin theta. The maximum force occurs when sin theta = 1, that is at 90 degrees, so Fmax = qvB. If the actual force is half of this maximum, then qvB sin theta = 1 over 2 qvB, which gives sin theta = 1 over 2. Therefore theta = 30 degrees, matching option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron emitted from a metal surface is 0.34eV. If the work function of the metal surface is 1.83eV,find the stopping potential.
questions.explanation: Stopping potential is related directly to the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons by eVs = KEmax. Since the maximum kinetic energy is already given as 0.34 eV, the stopping potential is numerically 0.34 V. The work function would only be needed if the photon energy had to be found first. Therefore the correct answer is 0.34 V, which corresponds to option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an alternating current given by I = 10sin (120π)t passes through a 12Ω resistor, the power dissipated in the resistor is
questions.explanation: The alternating current is I = 10 sin 120πt, so the peak current is 10 A. For a resistor, average power is P = Irms squared times R, with Irms = I0 divided by root 2 = 10 divided by root 2 A. Hence P = 10 squared over 2 x 12 = 50 x 12 = 600 W. The angular frequency does not affect the mean power in a pure resistor. So option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a semi conductor junction diode, as the depletion or barrier layer is forward-biased, the layer
questions.explanation: Forward bias opposes the built-in barrier potential of a p-n junction. As a result, majority carriers are pushed toward the junction and the depletion region becomes thinner. A narrower barrier allows charge carriers to cross more easily, so the current rises significantly. Reverse bias would do the opposite and widen the depletion layer. Therefore under forward bias, the depletion or barrier layer narrows, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The major difference between a pure semiconductor and a pure metal is that
options: while resistance of metals decrease with temperature , the reverse is the case for semiconductor
the resistance of metals increases with temperature, while for semiconductors, it is the reverse
metals have forbidden gaps while semiconductors have not
questions.explanation: The distinguishing property here is the temperature coefficient of resistance. In a metal, raising the temperature increases lattice vibrations and hinders electron flow, so resistance rises. In an intrinsic semiconductor, heating creates more charge carriers, so resistance falls. Therefore the correct statement is that metal resistance increases with temperature while semiconductor resistance decreases.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a nucleus is formed by bringing protons and neutrons together, the actual mass of the formed nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of the energy equivalent of this mass difference is the
questions.explanation: When separate protons and neutrons combine to form a nucleus, the nucleus has less mass than the sum of the free nucleon masses. The missing mass is the mass defect. By E = mc squared, its energy equivalent is the energy needed to separate the nucleus into its nucleons again. That energy is called the binding energy, so the correct option is binding energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A generator manufacturing company was contracted to produce an a.c dynamo but inadvertently produced a d.c dynamo. To correct this error, the
options: armature coil should be made of silver
commutator should be replaced with slip ring
commutator should be replaced with split rings
armature coil should be made of aluminium
questions.explanation: A d.c. dynamo uses a split ring commutator to make the external current unidirectional, while an a.c. generator uses slip rings so the alternating induced emf is delivered unchanged. Since the machine produced was d.c. instead of a.c., the correction is to replace the commutator with slip rings. The armature material is not the determining factor.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A radioisotope has a decay constant of 10\(^{-7}\)s\(^{-1}\). The average life of the radioisotope is
questions.explanation: Average life, or mean life, of a radioactive substance is the reciprocal of the decay constant: tau = 1 over lambda. With lambda = 10 to the power minus 7 per second, tau = 1 divided by 10 to the power minus 7 seconds = 10 to the power 7 seconds. So the correct value is 1.00 x 10^7 s. The 6.93 x 10^6 s option would correspond to half-life.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An a.c circuit of e.m.f 12V has a resistor of resistance 8Ω connected in series to an inductor of inductive reactance 16Ω and a capacitor capacitive reactance 10Ω. The current flow in the circuit is
questions.explanation: From the image, the resistor, inductor, and capacitor are in series. The net reactance is X = XL minus XC = 16 minus 10 = 6 ohms. The impedance is therefore Z = square root of R squared plus X squared = square root of 8 squared plus 6 squared = square root of 100 = 10 ohms. Hence the current is I = V over Z = 12 over 10 = 1.2 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: For semi conductor to have negative temperature coefficient of resistance implies that
options: their resistance is constantly changing with temperature
they have electrons and holes at high temperature
questions.explanation: A negative temperature coefficient means the resistance decreases as temperature increases. That is the normal behavior of semiconductors because heating frees more charge carriers, which improves conduction. So the statement that correctly expresses negative temperature coefficient is that their resistance decreases with temperature. The other options either state the opposite or describe consequences rather than the meaning itself.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: X rays can be used in the study of crystal structure because they
questions.explanation: Crystal spacing is of the order of 10 to the power minus 10 metre, so a wave used to probe crystal structure must have a comparable wavelength to produce diffraction. X rays satisfy this requirement because their wavelengths are extremely short. Their invisibility or high speed is irrelevant to crystal analysis. Therefore the correct reason is their extremely short wavelength.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A moving coil galvanometer has a full-scale deflection of 3A equivalent to 30o deflection. The sensitivity of the instrument is
questions.explanation: Galvanometer sensitivity is deflection per unit current. A current of 3 A gives a deflection of 30 degrees, so sensitivity = 30 divided by 3 = 10 degrees per ampere. Since the options are numerical only, the correct choice is 10.0. The data describe full-scale behavior directly, so no further conversion is needed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The particle and wave nature of matter are demonstrated in the equation
questions.explanation: The relation that links wave behavior to a particle property is the de Broglie equation. It states that wavelength equals Planck's constant divided by momentum, lambda = h over p. Wavelength is a wave quantity, while momentum is a particle quantity, so this equation expresses the dual nature of matter directly. The other formulas describe photons, ordinary waves, or diffraction geometry.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a reverse biased junction diode, current flows in by
questions.explanation: In reverse bias, the depletion region widens and majority carriers are prevented from crossing the junction. The tiny current that still exists is due to thermally generated minority carriers drifting across the junction. Therefore reverse current in a junction diode is carried by minority carriers, not by holes alone, electrons alone, or majority carriers.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a tuned radio receiver R, L, C series circuit for resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactance XL and XC respectively are related as
questions.explanation: At resonance in a series RLC circuit, the inductive reactance and capacitive reactance are equal in magnitude. Thus XL = XC, making the net reactance zero. The impedance is then reduced to the resistance alone, which gives the maximum current and the tuning condition used in radio receivers. Therefore the correct relation is XL equals XC.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Flourescent tubes produces light by the
options: refraction of light by gas molecules
thermal agitation of electron in the tubes
questions.explanation: A fluorescent tube works by electrical discharge through a low-pressure gas, which excites the gas atoms. These atoms emit mainly ultraviolet radiation, and the phosphor coating on the tube then converts that radiation into visible light. So the primary physical process responsible is excitation of gas molecules or atoms, not thermal agitation, refraction, or any form of solar energy conduction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The energy stored in an inductor of inductance 5mH when a current of 6A flows through it is
questions.explanation: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is E = one-half L I squared. Here L = 5 mH = 5 x 10 to the power minus 3 H and I = 6 A. So E = 0.5 x 5 x 10 to the power minus 3 x 36 = 0.09 J. This is 9.0 x 10 to the power minus 2 J, so the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is an electrolyte?
questions.explanation: An electrolyte conducts electricity because it contains ions that can move in solution. Grapefruit juice is acidic and contains dissolved ions, so it behaves as an electrolyte. Paraffin and alcohol do not ionize sufficiently, and sugar solution contains molecules rather than free ions in ordinary conditions. Hence grapefruit is the correct choice.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A steady current of 2A flows in a coil of emf 12V for 0.4s. A back emf of 3V was induced during this period. The stored energy in the loop that can be utilized is
questions.explanation: The useful energy stored in the magnetic field is the work done against the back emf, not the total electrical energy supplied. Thus E = back emf x current x time = 3 x 2 x 0.4 = 2.4 J. The remaining supply energy is dissipated elsewhere in the circuit. Therefore the stored energy that can be utilized is 2.4 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The instrument used for securing a large number of similar charges by induction is called
questions.explanation: The electrophorus is specifically designed to produce repeated charges of the same sign by electrostatic induction. It consists essentially of a charged insulating plate and a metal disc that can be alternately grounded and lifted to obtain similar charges many times. A capacitor stores charge, a proof plane samples charge, and an electroscope detects charge. Therefore electrophorus is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
If 16mA of current flows through a conductor in one second, the number of electron transported per seconds is

[1 electronic charge = 1.6 x 10-19C]
questions.explanation: Current is charge flow per second, so in one second the charge transferred is Q = It = 16 mA x 1 s = 16 x 10 to the power minus 3 C. The number of electrons is n = Q over e = 16 x 10 to the power minus 3 divided by 1.6 x 10 to the power minus 19 = 10 x 10 to the power 16 = 1.0 x 10^17. So option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Electrical appliances at home are normally earthed so that?
options: the appliances are maintained at a lower p.d than the earth
both the a.c and d.c sources can be used
a person touching the appliances is safe from electric shock
the appliances are maintained at a higher p.d than the earth
questions.explanation: Earthing connects the metal casing of an appliance to the ground through a low-resistance path. If a fault makes the casing live, current flows safely to earth rather than through a person touching the appliance. This keeps the casing near earth potential and reduces the risk of electric shock. Therefore the correct purpose is to protect the user from shock.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Given three capacitors 0.3μF, 0.5μF and 0.2μF, the joint capacitance when arranged to give minimum capacitance is
questions.explanation: To obtain the minimum equivalent capacitance, capacitors must be connected in series. Then 1 over C = 1 over 0.3 plus 1 over 0.5 plus 1 over 0.2 = 3.33 + 2 + 5 = 10.33 approximately. So C is about 1 over 10.33 = 0.097 microfarad, which rounds to 0.1 microfarad. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The difference between X-rays and gamma rays is that
options: x-rays are more penetrating than gamma rays
x-rays are electromagnetic radiations while gamma rays are negatively charged radiation
x-rays have higher frequencies than gamma rays
x-rays arise from energy changes in the electronic structure of atoms while gamma rays come from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Both X rays and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves, so they do not differ by charge, and either may occupy overlapping frequency ranges. The standard distinction is their origin. X rays are produced by electronic transitions or rapid electron deceleration outside the nucleus, while gamma rays come from transitions within the nucleus. Therefore the correct option is the one based on origin.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: To protect a material from the influnce of an external magnetic field, the materials should be kept
questions.explanation: Magnetic shielding requires a material with high magnetic permeability so that external magnetic field lines preferentially pass through the shield rather than the protected region. Soft iron has this property and is therefore commonly used. Copper and zinc are unsuitable for this purpose, and the exact geometric shape is less important than the material itself. So the soft iron ring is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the diagram above, the ratio of he electric power dissipated in the 6Ω and the 3Ω resistor respectively is
questions.explanation: From the diagram, the 6 ohm and 3 ohm resistors are connected in parallel across the same 12 V supply, so they have equal potential difference. Power in a resistor at fixed voltage is P = V squared over R. Therefore P6 to P3 = V squared over 6 to V squared over 3 = 1 over 6 to 1 over 3 = 1 to 2. Thus the correct ratio is 1:2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the angle between two vectors P and Q is Oº, the vectors are said to
questions.explanation: If the angle between two vectors is 0 degrees, they point in the same direction. Vectors with the same direction are parallel. They are not perpendicular, and the 45 degree and 60 degree options obviously contradict the given angle. Therefore the correct description is that the vectors are parallel.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body of mass 4kg is acted on by a constant force of 12N for 3 seconds. The kinetic energy gained by the body at the end of the time is
questions.explanation: The force gives the body an acceleration a = F over m = 12 over 4 = 3 m per s squared. Assuming it starts from rest, after 3 s its speed is v = at = 3 x 3 = 9 m per s. The kinetic energy gained is one-half m v squared = 0.5 x 4 x 81 = 162 J. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A machine whose efficiency is 60% has a velocity ratio of 5. If a force of 500N is applied to lift a load P, what is the magnitude of P?
questions.explanation: Efficiency equals mechanical advantage divided by velocity ratio. So mechanical advantage = efficiency x velocity ratio = 0.60 x 5 = 3. Mechanical advantage is also load over effort, hence load P = 3 x 500 N = 1500 N. Therefore the machine lifts a load of 1500 N, which matches option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Jet propelled aircraft

II. Rocket propulsion

III. The recoil of a gun

IV. A person walking

Which of the above is based on Newton's third law of motion
options: I, II, III, and IV only
questions.explanation: Newton's third law states that action and reaction are equal and opposite. A jet and a rocket move forward by expelling gas backward. A gun recoils backward when the bullet moves forward. A person walks because the foot pushes the ground backward and the ground pushes the person forward. All four examples fit the law, so the correct option includes I, II, III, and IV.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a hydraulic press , a force of 40N is applied on the effort piston of area 0.4m2. If the force exerted on the load piston is 400N, the area of the large piston is
questions.explanation: In a hydraulic press, pressure is transmitted equally, so F1 over A1 = F2 over A2. With F1 = 40 N, A1 = 0.4 m squared, and F2 = 400 N, the large piston area is A2 = F2A1 over F1 = 400 x 0.4 divided by 40 = 4 m squared. Therefore the area of the large piston is 4 m squared.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 100kg box is pushed along a road with force of 500N. If the box moves with a uniform velocity, the coefficient of friction between the box and the road is
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means zero net horizontal force, so the frictional force equals the applied force of 500 N. On a level road, the normal reaction is R = mg = 100 x 10 = 1000 N using g = 10 m per s squared. Hence the coefficient of friction is mu = friction over reaction = 500 over 1000 = 0.5. So option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: the diagram above shows forces 4N, 6N, 10N and 8N which act at a point O in the directions indicated. the net horizontal force is
questions.explanation: Using the diagram, resolve each force horizontally. The 10 N force acts fully to the right. The 8 N force at 60 degrees contributes 8 cos 60 = 4 N to the right. The 6 N force at 60 degrees below the horizontal contributes 6 cos 60 = 3 N to the right. The 4 N force acts left. Net horizontal force = 10 + 4 + 3 minus 4 = 13 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The earth is four times the size of the moon and the acceleration due to gravity on the earth is 80 times that on the moon. The ratio of the mass of the moon to that of the earth is
questions.explanation: Since g = GM over R squared, mass is proportional to gR squared. Therefore moon mass over earth mass equals moon gravity over earth gravity multiplied by moon radius squared over earth radius squared. Given earth gravity is 80 times moon gravity, gm over ge = 1 over 80. If earth is four times the size of the moon, take Re = 4Rm, so Rm squared over Re squared = 1 over 16. Hence Mm over Me = 1 over 80 x 1 over 16 = 1 over 1280.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In which of the following material media will sound travel fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest where particles interact most strongly and the medium is most rigid. In general, speed of sound is greatest in solids, less in liquids, and least in gases. Among oil, metal, gas, and water, only metal is a solid with very high rigidity. Therefore sound travels fastest in metal.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What types of mirror are capable of producing parallel beams of light such as those arising from the headlamps of a car?
questions.explanation: A parabolic mirror reflects light from a source at its focus into a beam of parallel rays. That is why car headlamps use a lamp placed near the focus of a parabolic reflector. Plane, cylindrical, and ordinary spherical mirrors do not produce such accurate collimation. Therefore the correct answer is parabolic mirrors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What happens to the rays in a parallel beam of light?
questions.explanation: In a parallel beam, the rays remain equidistant and do not meet at any finite point. In geometrical optics, such rays are described as meeting at infinity. They neither converge nor diverge as they travel ideally. Therefore the correct statement is that they meet at infinity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A ray of light makes an angle of 35o with a plane mirror. What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: The diagram and wording show that the incident ray makes 35 degrees with the mirror surface, not with the normal. The angle of incidence is therefore 90 minus 35 = 55 degrees. By the law of reflection, angle of reflection equals angle of incidence. Hence the angle of reflection is 55 degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A person can focus an object only when it lies within 200cm from him. Which spectacles should be used to increase his maximum distance of distinct vision infinity
questions.explanation: If the person can see clearly only up to 200 cm, then distant objects cannot be focused, which indicates short-sightedness. To see objects at infinity, incoming parallel rays must be made to appear to come from the person's far point. A concave lens diverges light in exactly that way, so it is the correct spectacle lens.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The pitch of a sound note depends on
questions.explanation: Pitch is determined by the frequency of a sound. A higher frequency is heard as a higher pitch, while a lower frequency is heard as a lower pitch. Timbre or quality describes the character of the sound, and harmonics influence that quality, but they do not replace frequency as the primary determinant of pitch. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If u is the object distance and v the image distance, which of the following expressions gives the linear magnification produced by a convex lens of focal length f?
questions.explanation: Linear magnification for a lens is m = v over u. Using the lens formula 1 over f = 1 over u + 1 over v, rearrange to get u = fv over v minus f. Substituting into m gives m = v divided by fv over v minus f = v minus f over f = v over f minus 1. Therefore the correct expression is v over f minus 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The refractive index of the medium M in the diagram above is
questions.explanation: From the diagram, the 30 degree label above the surface is with the surface, so the angle of incidence to the normal is 60 degrees. The 60 degree label in medium M is also with the surface, so the angle of refraction to the normal is 30 degrees. Applying Snell's law for air to medium M gives n = sin 60 divided by sin 30 = square root of 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When left in a freezer, a bottle full of water cracks on freezing into ice because of the
options: increase in the volume of water
decrease in the volume of water
questions.explanation: Water expands when it freezes, unlike most liquids. If a bottle is completely full, this increase in volume during freezing creates a large pressure against the walls of the bottle. That pressure can crack the bottle. Therefore the reason is the increase in the volume of water on freezing.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The change in volume when 450kg of ice is completely melted is [density of ice = 900 kgm\(^{-3}\), density of water = 1000 kgm\(^{-3}\)]
questions.explanation: Volume equals mass divided by density. The volume of 450 kg of ice is 450 divided by 900 = 0.50 m cubed. After melting, the water volume is 450 divided by 1000 = 0.45 m cubed. The change in volume is therefore 0.50 minus 0.45 = 0.05 m cubed. So the correct answer is 0.05 m cubed.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Tea pots are often silver-coated to prevent heat loss by
questions.explanation: Silvered or polished surfaces are poor emitters and poor absorbers of thermal radiation. Coating a teapot with silver therefore reduces heat loss mainly by radiation. It does not directly stop heat transfer by conduction through the solid or convection in the surrounding air. Hence the correct answer is radiation only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Wavelength

II. Medium of propagation

III. Wave velocity

IV. Frequency

V. Energy

Which of the above are used for characterizing waves?
questions.explanation: Waves are commonly characterized by measurable quantities such as wavelength, wave speed, and frequency. The medium of propagation is not a universal defining property because some waves, like electromagnetic waves, do not need a material medium. Energy is associated with a wave, but it is not the standard set used to specify the wave itself. Therefore I, III, and IV are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 50W electric heater is used to heat a metal block of mass 5kg. If in 10 minutes a temperature rise of 12oC is achieved, the specific heat capacity of the metal is
questions.explanation: The heater supplies energy E = Pt = 50 x 10 x 60 = 30000 J in 10 minutes. This energy raises the block temperature by 12 degrees, so E = mc delta theta = 5 x c x 12 = 60c. Hence c = 30000 divided by 60 = 500 J per kg per K. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Transverse waves can be distinguished from longitudinal waves using the characteristic of
questions.explanation: Polarization distinguishes transverse waves from longitudinal waves. A transverse wave can vibrate in different planes perpendicular to its direction of travel, so it can be polarized. A longitudinal wave vibrates along its direction of travel and cannot be polarized. Reflection, refraction, and diffraction can occur for both types, so they do not provide the distinction.

questions.subject: physics
