questions.text: A man exerts a pressure of 2.8 x 103Nm-2 on the ground and has 4 x 10-2m2 of his feet in contact with the ground. The weight of the man is
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, so the man's weight is F = PA. Substituting P = 2.8 x 10 to the power 3 N per m squared and A = 4 x 10 to the power minus 2 m squared gives F = 2.8 x 10 to the power 3 x 4 x 10 to the power minus 2 = 11.2 x 10 = 112 N. Therefore the correct answer is 112 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Marching soldiers crossing a suspension bridge are usually advised to break their steps to avoid damaging the bridge owing to
questions.explanation: When soldiers march in step, they apply a periodic driving force to the bridge. If that driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the bridge, the oscillations build up to dangerously large amplitude. This effect is resonance. Breaking step prevents a steady periodic forcing and reduces the risk of structural damage, so resonance is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A thin converging lens has a power of 4.0 diopters determined its focal length.
questions.explanation: The power of a lens is related to focal length by P = 1 divided by f when f is in metres. With P = 4.0 dioptres, f = 1 divided by 4.0 = 0.25 m. Because the lens is converging, the focal length is positive, so the sign is consistent. Therefore the correct option is 0.25 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A real image three times the size of an object is formed 24cm from a converging mirror. what is the focal length of the mirror.
questions.explanation: For a converging mirror, a real image is inverted, so the magnification magnitude is 3. Hence image distance divided by object distance equals 3. With v = 24 cm, the object distance is u = 24 divided by 3 = 8 cm. Using the mirror formula, 1 divided by f = 1 divided by 8 + 1 divided by 24 = 1 divided by 6, so f = 6 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The pair of physical quantities consisting of vectors only are
questions.explanation: Momentum and acceleration are vectors, but power, distance, and speed are scalars. Displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Torque is also treated as a vector quantity in school physics because it has a directed turning effect. Therefore the only pair consisting entirely of vectors is displacement and torque.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In an ideal wheel an axle system, R stand for the radius of the wheel and r is the radius of the axle. the mechanical advantage is
questions.explanation: In an ideal wheel and axle, mechanical advantage equals velocity ratio because no energy is lost. The effort moves through the circumference of the wheel, 2 pi R, while the load moves through the circumference of the axle, 2 pi r. Their ratio is 2 pi R divided by 2 pi r, which simplifies to R divided by r. So the mechanical advantage is R divided by r.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In an a.c circuit that contains only a capacitor, the voltage lags behind the current by
questions.explanation: For a pure capacitor in an alternating current circuit, the current reaches its maximum a quarter cycle before the voltage does. That means current leads voltage by 90 degrees. Reversing the same statement, the voltage lags behind the current by 90 degrees. Therefore the correct option is 90 degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: the time it will take a certain radioactive material with a half-life of 50 days to reduce to 1/32of its original number is
questions.explanation: A reduction to 1 over 32 of the original amount means the material has undergone five halvings, because 1 over 32 equals 1 over 2 to the power 5. Each half-life is 50 days, so the total time is 5 times 50 days = 250 days. Hence the correct answer is 250 days.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When impurities are added to semi-conductors, the conductivity of the semi-conductor
questions.explanation: Adding suitable impurities to a semiconductor is called doping. The impurity atoms supply extra electrons or create holes, increasing the number of charge carriers available for conduction. Since electrical conductivity depends strongly on carrier concentration, controlled doping increases conductivity. Therefore the correct option is increases.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A silicon material is dopped with an element of a certain group and an n-type semi-conductor is formed. the most likely group of the element is
questions.explanation: Silicon is a group IV element with four valence electrons. To form an n-type semiconductor, it is doped with a pentavalent impurity so that one electron is left over after bonding. That extra electron becomes a mobile charge carrier, making electrons the majority carriers. Therefore the dopant most likely belongs to group V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The charge carriers in gasses are
questions.explanation: Conduction in gases occurs only after ionization produces mobile charged particles. The gas then contains free electrons and ions, both of which can move under an electric field and carry charge. Holes are associated with semiconductors, not gases. Therefore the correct answer is electrons and ions.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The ray which causes gas molecules to glow is known as
questions.explanation: In a discharge tube, cathode rays are streams of electrons emitted from the cathode. When these electrons collide with gas molecules, they excite the molecules, which then emit light and produce a glow. This is the standard school-level explanation of gas glow in such tubes. Therefore the correct option is cathode ray.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A transformer is rated 240v. If the primary coil is 4000 turns and the secondary voltage 12v, determine the number of turns in the secondary coil.
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, the ratio of voltages equals the ratio of turns: Vp divided by Vs = Np divided by Ns. With Vp = 240 V, Vs = 12 V, and Np = 4000, the secondary turns are Ns = 4000 times 12 divided by 240 = 200. The result is a count of turns, not a voltage. Therefore the correct answer is 200.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The current in a reverse-biased junction is due to?
questions.explanation: In reverse bias, the depletion region widens and the majority carriers are pulled away from the junction, so they contribute negligibly to current. The small current that still flows is due to thermally generated minority carriers that cross the junction. This is the reverse saturation current. Therefore the correct answer is minority carriers.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: which of the following materials is a conductor?
questions.explanation: Glass, wax, and plastic are electrical insulators under ordinary conditions because they do not provide many free charge carriers. Sodium is a metal, and metals conduct electricity through mobile electrons in their structure. Therefore, among the listed materials, sodium is the conductor.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When the temperature difference between the wet and dry bulbs of a hygrometer is high, this indicates that
questions.explanation: A large difference between wet-bulb and dry-bulb temperatures means the wet bulb is cooling strongly by evaporation. Strong evaporation happens when the surrounding air is relatively dry and can still absorb much more water vapour. Therefore a high wet-dry bulb difference indicates low relative humidity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 3m3 volume of liquid W of density 200kgm3 is mixed with another liquid L of volume 7m3 and density 150kgm-3. the density of mixture is?
questions.explanation: Density of the mixture equals total mass divided by total volume, assuming the volumes simply add. The first liquid has mass 200 times 3 = 600 kg, and the second has mass 150 times 7 = 1050 kg. Total mass is 1650 kg and total volume is 10 cubic metres. Therefore density = 1650 divided by 10 = 165 kg per cubic metre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A body of mass 36kg falls through a viscous liquid which offers a drag force of 260N on the body. The upthrust on the body at terminal velocity is?

[g = 10ms\(^2\)]
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the net force on the body is zero, so the downward weight equals the sum of the upward drag force and upthrust. The weight is mg = 36 times 10 = 360 N. Given drag = 260 N, the upthrust is 360 - 260 = 100 N upward. Therefore the correct answer is 100 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The process whereby the molecules of different substances move randomly is called?
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the spontaneous random intermingling of molecules of different substances due to their constant motion. Capillarity concerns liquid rise in narrow tubes, surface tension concerns the liquid surface, and osmosis is a special case involving solvent movement through a semipermeable membrane. Therefore the correct process is diffusion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. reproducibility

II. Sensibility

III. High thermal capacity

iv. High accuracy

The quantities of a good thermometer include?
questions.explanation: A good thermometer should be reproducible, sensitive, and accurate so that it gives consistent, noticeable, and correct readings. High thermal capacity is undesirable because the thermometer would absorb more heat from the body being measured and respond more slowly. Hence statements I, II, and IV are correct, while III is not.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The process whereby a liquid turns spontaneously into vapour is called?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process in which molecules escape spontaneously from the surface of a liquid to form vapour, even below the boiling point. Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a definite temperature, sublimation is solid directly to vapour, and regelation refers to pressure melting and refreezing. Therefore the correct answer is evaporation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Melting

II. Boiling

III. Refraction

IV. Conduction

Which combination of the above is evident of the molecular nature of matter?
questions.explanation: Melting and boiling are explained by molecular motion and changes in intermolecular forces, so they support the molecular nature of matter. Conduction in matter also depends on transfer through particles. Refraction, however, is mainly an optical wave phenomenon and is not direct evidence for the particulate structure of matter. Therefore the correct combination is I, II and IV only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When very hot water is poured into two identical thin and thick glass tumblers in equal volumes, the thick one cracks because?
options: of the even expansion of glass
glass is a good conductor of heat
of the uneven expansion of glass
questions.explanation: When very hot water is poured into thick glass, the inner surface heats and expands sooner than the outer surface. Because glass is a poor conductor, this temperature difference persists long enough to create internal stress. The resulting unequal expansion can crack the tumbler. Therefore the thick tumbler cracks because of uneven expansion of the glass.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Satellite communication network makes use of?
questions.explanation: Satellite communication uses electromagnetic waves that can travel through vacuum between Earth and the satellite. In practice these are radio waves, commonly in the microwave part of the radio spectrum. Sound cannot travel through vacuum, and visible or infrared light are not the standard school-level answer here. Therefore the correct option is radio wave.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric device is rated 2000 W, 250 v. The correct fuse rating of the device is?
questions.explanation: The operating current is found from P = VI, so I = 2000 divided by 250 = 8 A. A fuse should be rated slightly above the normal working current so that it does not melt during ordinary use but still provides protection when current becomes excessive. Therefore the suitable fuse rating from the options is 9 A.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The north pole of a magnet can never be separated from the south pole because of the property knowledge as?
questions.explanation: A permanent magnet always has both a north and a south pole. If it is cut into pieces, each piece becomes a smaller magnet with its own pair of poles rather than yielding an isolated pole. This behavior expresses the dipole nature of magnetism in ordinary materials. Therefore the relevant property is magnetic dipole.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A car battery rated 45 A H is charged with a charger whose rating is 2.5A.How long will it take to charge the battery full?
questions.explanation: Battery capacity in ampere-hour divided by charging current in ampere gives the charging time in hours, ignoring inefficiency. With a capacity of 45 A h and a charging current of 2.5 A, time = 45 divided by 2.5 = 18 h. Therefore the full-charge time is 18 hours.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electric field intensity in a place where a charge of 10-10c experiences a force of 0.4N is?
questions.explanation: Electric field intensity is force per unit charge: E = F divided by q. Substituting F = 0.4 N and q = 10 to the minus 10 C gives E = 0.4 divided by 10 to the minus 10 = 4.0 times 10 to the power 9 N per C. Therefore the correct answer is 4.0 x 10^9 N C^-1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two charged particles are projected into a region where there is a magnetic field perpendicular to their velocities. if the charges are deflected in opposite directions, which of the following statements is true of the charge?
options: the charge must be of opposite sign
positive charges are more in number
the charges are of the same sign
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by F = q times v cross B. For particles entering the same magnetic field with comparable velocity direction, the sense of deflection depends on the sign of q. If the deflections are opposite, the charges must have opposite signs. Therefore the correct statement is that the charges are of opposite sign.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
The resistance of a piece of wire of length 20m has crossed-sectional area 8 x 10\(^{-6}\)m\(^2\)is?

[Resistivity of the wire = 4 x 10\(^{-7}\) Ω m]
questions.explanation: The resistance of a wire is R = rho L divided by A. Using rho = 4 x 10^-7 ohm metre, L = 20 m, and A = 8 x 10^-6 square metre, R = (4 x 10^-7 x 20) divided by (8 x 10^-6) = 8 x 10^-6 divided by 8 x 10^-6 = 1.0 ohm. Therefore the correct answer is 1.0 ohm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A uniform solid cube material 10cm on each side of mass 700g is submerged in water. which of the following best described the behavior of the cube water?
options: the cube will melt after a period of time
the cube will sink in water
the cube will rest at an equilibrium position in water
questions.explanation: The cube has side 10 cm, so its volume is 10 x 10 x 10 = 1000 cubic centimetres, which is 1.0 x 10^-3 cubic metre. Its mass is 700 g = 0.7 kg, giving density 0.7 divided by 1.0 x 10^-3 = 700 kg per cubic metre. Since this is less than water's density, the cube will float.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At low humidity in an environment, the human skin is usually?
questions.explanation: Low humidity means the surrounding air contains little water vapour and encourages evaporation from the skin. Increased evaporation removes moisture from the skin surface, leaving it dry. Dry skin usually feels coarse rather than smooth. Therefore, in low humidity, the human skin is usually dry and rough.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the relative density of gold is 19.2, the volume of 2.4kg of gold is?
questions.explanation: Relative density 19.2 means the density of gold is 19.2 times the density of water, so rho = 19.2 x 1000 = 1.92 x 10^4 kg per cubic metre. The volume is V = m divided by rho = 2.4 divided by 1.92 x 10^4 = 1.25 x 10^-4 cubic metre. Therefore the correct option is 1.25 x 10^-4 m3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The thermometric property of a constant volume thermometer is?
questions.explanation: In a constant-volume gas thermometer, the gas is prevented from expanding, so its volume is fixed. When the temperature changes under that condition, the measurable quantity that changes is the gas pressure. Thus the thermometric property used is change in pressure, not change in volume or length.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
An immersion heater rated 2.0A, 240V is used to boil water from temperature 52°c to 100°c. If the mass of the water is 2.5kg. determine the time taken to boil the water.

[specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 x 103 jkg-1 k-1]
questions.explanation: The heat needed is Q = mc delta theta = 2.5 x 4.2 x 10^3 x (100 - 52). Since the temperature rise is 48 K, Q = 5.04 x 10^5 J. The heater power is P = VI = 240 x 2.0 = 480 W. Therefore the time is t = Q divided by P = 5.04 x 10^5 divided by 480 = 1.05 x 10^3 s.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The thermos flask is designed to?
options: prevent heat loss or gain by conduction, convection and radiation
prevent heat gain by conduction, convection and radiation
prevent heat lost by conduction, convention and radiation
questions.explanation: A thermos flask is designed to reduce heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation. Its vacuum and insulating structure work in either direction: they slow heat from entering cold contents and also slow heat from leaving hot contents. Therefore the most complete statement is that it prevents heat loss or gain by conduction, convection and radiation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: what is likely to happen if the glass of a thermometer expands more upon heating than the liquid inside?
options: the liquid will rise up in the stem
the liquid will go down in the stem
questions.explanation: A liquid-in-glass thermometer works properly only when the liquid expands more than the glass. If the glass expands more on heating, the bulb and stem volume increase faster than the liquid volume does. Relative to the stem, the liquid level would then fall instead of rise. Therefore the liquid will go down in the stem.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A drop of petrol makes a finger colder than a drop of water would because?
options: petrol takes its latent heat of veporization from the finger
petrol takes its latent heat of fusion from the finger
water is more viscious than petrol
water has higher surface tension dan petrol
questions.explanation: Petrol evaporates more readily than water. During evaporation, molecules escaping from the liquid require latent heat of vaporization, which is taken from the finger and its surroundings. This heat loss cools the skin, making petrol feel colder than water. Latent heat of fusion concerns melting and is irrelevant here. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A cell of internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor R. The condition for maximum power transfer is?
questions.explanation: For a source with internal resistance r supplying a load resistance R, the power delivered to the load is greatest when the load resistance matches the internal resistance. This is the maximum power transfer condition. Therefore the correct relation is R = r.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The production and type of charge of a body can only be accounted for by the?
questions.explanation: Ordinary charging of bodies is explained by transfer of electrons from one body to another. A body becomes negatively charged by gaining electrons and positively charged by losing them. Protons remain bound in nuclei and neutrons have no charge, so neither explains the type of charge acquired. Therefore the correct answer is deficiency or surplus of electrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The main purpose of the transformer in an a.c radio set is to?
options: convert energy from a.c to d.c
questions.explanation: In a radio set powered from an a.c. source, the transformer is used mainly to change the mains voltage to a lower value suitable for the circuitry. It does not convert a.c. to d.c.; that is the job of a rectifier. It also does not increase power. Therefore the correct answer is step down the voltage.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric heater with a p.d of 240 V connected across its terminals has a total resistance of 960Ω. find the power rating of the heater.
questions.explanation: For a resistor connected across a potential difference, power is P = V squared divided by R. Substituting V = 240 V and R = 960 ohm gives P = 240 squared divided by 960 = 57600 divided by 960 = 60 W. Therefore the heater power rating is 60.00 W.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an a.c. voltage is applied to a capacitor, no power is consumed because the current
options: and voltage are 180° out of phase
questions.explanation: Average power in an a.c. circuit is proportional to VI cos phi, where phi is the phase angle between current and voltage. In a pure capacitor, current leads voltage by 90 degrees, so phi = 90 degrees and cos 90 degrees = 0. Hence no average power is consumed. Therefore the correct option is that current leads voltage by 90 degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electrolyte in the Nickei-iron (Nife) accumulator is
questions.explanation: The nickel-iron accumulator, also called the Nife or Edison cell, uses an alkaline electrolyte. The electrolyte is potassium hydroxide solution. Dilute sulphuric acid belongs to the lead-acid accumulator, while ammonium chloride is associated with the Leclanche cell. Therefore the correct answer is potassium hydroxide solution.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: During electrolysis, 2.0 g of a metal is deposited using a current of 0.5 A in 3 hours. The mass of the same metal which can be deposited using a current of 1.5 A in 1 hour is?
questions.explanation: By Faraday's law, the deposited mass is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed, and charge equals current times time. In the first case, current times time is 0.5 x 3 = 1.5 ampere-hour and deposits 2.0 g. In the second case, 1.5 x 1 = 1.5 ampere-hour as well, so the same mass, 2.0 g, is deposited.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a certain a.c supply is connected to a lamp, it lights with the same brightness as it does with a 12 V d.c battery. Then r.m.s value of the a.c supply is?
questions.explanation: The root-mean-square value of an alternating voltage is the direct voltage that would produce the same heating effect, and therefore the same brightness, in a resistive lamp. Since the lamp glows the same as with a 12 V direct battery, the a.c. supply must have an r.m.s. value of 12.0 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An ammeter of resistance 5Ω has a full-scale deflection when a current of 50 mA flows in it. The value of the resistor required to adapt it to measure a current of 5 A is?
questions.explanation: The meter has resistance 5 ohm and full-scale current 0.05 A, so the voltage across it at full scale is 0.05 x 5 = 0.25 V. To measure 5 A total, the shunt carries 5.00 - 0.05 = 4.95 A at the same 0.25 V. Thus shunt resistance = 0.25 divided by 4.95 about 0.0505 ohm, which rounds to 0.05 ohm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The motion of smoke particles from a chimney is typical of?
questions.explanation: Smoke particles move in an irregular, unpredictable way because they are continually buffeted by surrounding air molecules. This kind of zigzag motion is random motion and is commonly described as Brownian-type behavior. It is not circular, rotational, or oscillatory. Therefore the correct option is random motion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
If the radius of the Earth is 6.4 x 10\(^6\)m, the escape velocity of a satellite from the Earth is?

[g = 10 ms\(^-2\)]
questions.explanation: Escape velocity from the Earth’s surface is obtained by equating kinetic energy to the work needed against gravity, giving v = sqrt(2gR). With g = 10 m s^-2 and R = 6.4 x 10^6 m, 2gR = 1.28 x 10^8. Taking the square root gives 1.13 x 10^4 m s^-1. The arithmetic, power of ten, and unit match option 0 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The component of vector X along the direction of vector Y is zero when
options: X and Y are in opposite directions to each other
X is at an angle of 45° to Y
X and Y are parallel to each other
questions.explanation: The component of X along Y is the projection X cos theta, where theta is the angle between the vectors. For that component to be zero, cos theta must be zero, which happens at 90 degrees. Vectors in opposite directions give cos 180 degrees = -1, not zero. Therefore the only correct condition is that X is perpendicular to Y.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The correct unit of energy density is?
questions.explanation: Energy density means energy per unit volume. One joule is kg m^2 s-2, and one cubic metre is m^3. Dividing gives kg m^2 s-2 over m^3 = kg m-1 s-2. The metre power is negative one after subtraction, which rules out the other options. So the correct SI unit of energy density is kg m-1 s-2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
The energy associated with the emitted photon when a mercury atom changes from one state to another is 3.3 ev. calculate the frequency of the photon.

[e = 1.6 x 10-19c; h = 6.6 x 10-34js]
questions.explanation: Photon energy is related to frequency by E = hf. First convert 3.3 eV to joules: 3.3 x 1.6 x 10-19 = 5.28 x 10-19 J. Then f = E/h = 5.28 x 10-19 divided by 6.6 x 10-34 = 0.8 x 10^15 Hz = 8.0 x 10^14 Hz. The sign, conversion, and power of ten are all consistent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The process through which free electrons leave the surface of hot metal is known as?
questions.explanation: When a metal is heated strongly, some electrons gain enough energy to overcome the surface barrier and leave the metal. That specific heat-caused emission process is called thermionic emission. Photo emission requires incident light, not just heating, while electron emission is only a general description. Therefore the precise term asked for is thermionic emission.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The battery connection that permits current to flow across a p-n junction is called?
questions.explanation: A p-n junction conducts appreciably when it is forward biased. In forward bias, the external battery reduces the depletion barrier so majority charge carriers can cross the junction. Reverse bias enlarges the barrier and strongly suppresses current. Amplification and rectification describe circuit functions, not the battery connection itself. Therefore the correct option is forward biased.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: One of the properties of gamma rays is that they are?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are electromagnetic radiation, not material particles like alpha or beta emissions. Electromagnetic waves carry no electric charge, so they are neutral. They also have zero rest mass, so calling them massive would be wrong in this context. Therefore the listed property that correctly describes gamma rays is that they are neutral.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A radioactive element has a half life of 4 days. The fraction that has decayed in 16 days is?
questions.explanation: A half-life of 4 days means the undecayed fraction halves every 4 days. In 16 days, there are 16 divided by 4 = 4 half-lives. The remaining fraction is 1 over 2^4 = 1/16. The fraction that has decayed is therefore 1 - 1/16 = 15/16. The question asks for decayed fraction, not the portion left.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The theory of electronic conduction in solids, which satisfactorily explains the properties of conductors, insulators and semi-conductor,is?
questions.explanation: Band theory explains electrical behavior in solids by treating electron energies as allowed bands separated by forbidden gaps. Conductors have overlapping or partly filled bands, insulators have large band gaps, and semiconductors have small gaps. That framework accounts for the listed classes of materials, unlike the distractors. Therefore the correct theory is band theory.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. The number of neutrons released exceeds the number that caused the fission.

II. There is loss of mass.

III. Energy is produced.

IV. Smaller nuclei merge to form larger nuclei

which of the statement above are correct about nuclear fission?
questions.explanation: In nuclear fission, a heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei, often after absorbing one neutron. More neutrons are usually released than were used to trigger the event, so statement I is true. There is also a mass defect, making II true, and the missing mass appears as energy, so III is true. Statement IV describes fusion, not fission.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A certain manufacturer wishes to make an n-type semiconductor. Which materials would he select for doping?
questions.explanation: An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping with pentavalent impurities, which contribute extra electrons. Arsenic and antimony are both group V elements and therefore act as donor impurities. Boron, aluminium, and indium are trivalent and instead create p-type material by producing holes. So the only suitable pair for n-type doping is arsenic and antimony.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A p-n junction diode is used as?
options: a rectifier in a d.c circuit
an anplifier in an a.c circuit
a rectifier in an a.c circuit
questions.explanation: A p-n junction diode allows current mainly in one direction, which makes it useful for rectification. Rectification is needed in an alternating-current circuit to convert AC into a unidirectional current. A diode is not itself an amplifier, and a direct-current circuit does not require rectification in the ordinary sense. Therefore the correct use listed is a rectifier in an AC circuit.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object placed 10cm from a concave mirror of focal length 5cm would have its image
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, radius of curvature R equals 2f. With focal length 5 cm, R = 10 cm. Since the object is placed 10 cm from the mirror, it is at the center of curvature. An object at the center of curvature forms its image at the center of curvature as well. Therefore the correct option is at the centre of curvature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A submarine is observed to rise from a real depth of 80 m to 60 m in water. Calculate the change in apparent depth.

[Refraction index of water \(\frac{4}{3}\)]
questions.explanation: Apparent depth in water is real depth divided by refractive index. Initially, 80 m in water appears as 80 x 3/4 = 60 m. After the submarine rises to a real depth of 60 m, its apparent depth becomes 60 x 3/4 = 45 m. The change in apparent depth is 60 - 45 = 15 m. The arithmetic and interpretation both fit option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Non-luminous object can be seen because they
questions.explanation: A non-luminous object does not produce its own light. It is visible only when light from another source falls on it and some of that light is reflected into the eye. Being near or polished may affect brightness or visibility, but those are not the fundamental reason it can be seen. Therefore the correct answer is that non-luminous objects reflect light.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The wavelength of the first overtone of a note in a closed pipe of length 33 cm is?
questions.explanation: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics. The first overtone is therefore the third harmonic. For the third harmonic in a closed pipe, L = 3 lambda over 4, so lambda = 4L over 3. Substituting L = 33 cm gives lambda = 4 x 33 divided by 3 = 44 cm. The wavelength is thus 44 cm, matching option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A person can focus objects when they lie beyond 75 cm from his eyes. The focal length of the lens required to reduce his least distance of distinct vision to 25 cm is?
questions.explanation: This person’s near point is 75 cm, and the lens should allow an object at 25 cm to appear virtually at 75 cm. Using the thin-lens formula with sign convention, u = -25 cm and v = -75 cm. Then 1/f = 1/v - 1/u = -1/75 + 1/25 = 2/75, so f = 37.5 cm. That matches option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The unit of moment of a couple can be expressed in?
questions.explanation: The moment of a couple is the product of one of the forces and the perpendicular distance between the forces’ lines of action. Force is measured in newtons and distance in metres, so the unit is newton metre, N m. Although dimensionally the same as joule, it is not written as joule because it represents turning effect, not energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A gramophone record takes 5s to reach its constant angular velocity of 4\(\pi\) rads-1 from rest. Find its constant angular acceleration.
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is change in angular velocity divided by time. The record starts from rest, so the initial angular velocity is zero and the final angular velocity is 4 pi rad s-1 after 5 s. Hence alpha = 4 pi divided by 5 = 0.8 pi rad s-2. Both the arithmetic and unit agree with option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A car of mass 1500 kg goes round a circular curve of radius 50m at a speed of 40 ms-1. The magnitude of the centripetal force on the car is ?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is F = mv^2/r. With m = 1500 kg, v = 40 m s-1, and r = 50 m, v^2 = 1600 and F = 1500 x 1600 divided by 50 = 48000 N. In scientific notation that is 4.8 x 10^4 N. The power of ten and unit are correct, so option 0 is the defensible answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
Two spheres of masses 5.0 kg and 10.0 kg are 0.3 m apart. Calculate the force of attraction between them?

[G = 6.67 X 10-11 Nm2 Kg\(^{-2}\)]
questions.explanation: Newton’s law of gravitation gives F = Gm1m2/r^2. Substituting G = 6.67 x 10-11, m1 = 5.0 kg, m2 = 10.0 kg, and r = 0.3 m gives F = 6.67 x 10-11 x 50 divided by 0.09 = 3.335 x 10-9 divided by 0.09 about 3.71 x 10-8 N. This matches option 1 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A machine has a velocity ratio of 4. if it requires 800 N to overcome a load of 1600 N,what is the efficiency of the machine?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage is load divided by effort, so MA = 1600/800 = 2. Efficiency equals MA divided by velocity ratio times 100 percent. With VR = 4, efficiency = 2/4 x 100 = 50 percent. The calculation uses the correct machine relation and clearly distinguishes velocity ratio from mechanical advantage. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A reservoir 500 m deep is filled with a fluid of density 850 kgm-3. If the atmospheric pressure is 1.05 x 105 Nm-2, the pressure at the bottom of the reservoir is.

[g = 10ms-2]
questions.explanation: The pressure at the bottom is the absolute pressure, found from P = Patm + rho g h. Using rho = 850 kg m-3, g = 10 m s-2, and h = 500 m gives rho g h = 850 x 10 x 500 = 4.25 x 10^6 Pa. Adding atmospheric pressure 1.05 x 10^5 Pa gives 4.355 x 10^6 Pa, which rounds to 4.36 x 10^6 Pa.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A piece of iron weights 250 N in air and 200 N in a liquid of density 1000 kgm-3. the volume of the iron is?
questions.explanation: The apparent loss of weight in the liquid is the upthrust: 250 N - 200 N = 50 N. By Archimedes’ principle, upthrust = rho g V. Thus V = 50 divided by 1000 x 10 = 50/10000 = 5.0 x 10-3 m^3. The numerical value fits option 0. The correct unit is cubic metre, not reciprocal cubic metre.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A clinical thermometer is different from other mercury in glass thermometers owing to
options: the grade of mercury used in it
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer has a constriction, or kink, in the narrow tube just above the bulb. This prevents the mercury thread from falling back immediately when the thermometer is removed, so the reading can be taken after use. The distinction is not a special mercury grade, unusual stem length, or a wide temperature range. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Use a liquid with a high melting point.

II. use a liquid of high volume expansivity.

III. use a capillary tube of large diameter.

which of the above best describes how the sensitivity of a liquid-in-glass thermometer can be enhanced?
questions.explanation: Thermometer sensitivity means a small temperature change should cause a large movement of the liquid column. That is enhanced by using a liquid with high volume expansivity, so statement II is correct. A large capillary diameter would reduce the rise for the same expansion, making III false. A high melting point is not the relevant requirement for sensitivity. Therefore II only is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
2 kg of water is heated with a heating coil which draws 3.5 A from a 200 V mains for 2 minutes. what is the increase in temperature of the water?

[specific heat capacity of water = 4200 jkg -1k-1]
questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied is E = VIt = 200 x 3.5 x 120 = 84000 J, since 2 minutes equals 120 s. The temperature rise is found from E = mc delta T, so delta T = 84000 divided by 2 x 4200 = 10. A rise of 10 K is numerically the same as 10 degrees Celsius. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The blade of a hoe feel colder to touch in the morning than the wooden handle because the
options: handle is a better conductor of heat than blade
handle contains stored energy in form of heat
blade is a better conductor of heat than the handle
blade is placed at a lower temperature than the heat
questions.explanation: Both the metal blade and wooden handle may be at the same temperature, but the blade feels colder because iron conducts heat away from the hand much faster than wood. The sensation of cold depends on rate of heat loss from the skin, not merely on temperature alone. Therefore the blade is a better conductor of heat than the handle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. They should be identical

II. They should originate from the same source.

III. They should be coherent.

IV. They should be monochromatic.

from the statements above, the conditions for two waves to interfere are?
questions.explanation: For a sustained and clear interference pattern, the waves should be coherent, effectively monochromatic, and usually derived from the same source so their phase relationship remains fixed. They do not need to be identical in every respect; that statement is stronger than necessary. Hence statements II, III, and IV are the required conditions, corresponding to option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a large telecommunications auditorium, perforated absorbent materials are used to line the ceiling so as to
options: Increase the reverberation of sound in the hall
increase the amount of echo in the hall
reduce the hight of the ceiling from the floor
reduce the reverberation of sound in the hall
questions.explanation: Perforated absorbent materials reduce the amount of sound reflected repeatedly from the ceiling and other surfaces. This lowers reverberation time and improves the clarity of speech and music in a large hall. Such materials are used to suppress excessive persistence of sound, not to increase echo or make the ceiling effectively lower. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The phenomenon of light bending round an obstacle is?
questions.explanation: The bending or spreading of light around the edge of an obstacle is diffraction. Refraction is bending when light passes from one medium to another, reflection is the return of light from a surface, and polarization concerns the orientation of vibrations. Since the question specifically mentions bending round an obstacle, diffraction is the correct phenomenon.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The instrument used by designers to obtain different color pattern is called?
questions.explanation: A kaleidoscope forms many changing symmetrical colour patterns by multiple reflections between inclined mirrors. That is why it is associated with design and pattern generation. A periscope is for viewing over obstacles, a sextant measures angular positions, and an episcope projects images of opaque objects. Therefore the instrument asked for is the kaleidoscope.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A glass plate 0.9cm thick has a refractive index of 1.50. How long does it take for a pulse of light to pass through the plate?

[c = 3.0 x 10\(^8\) ms-1]
questions.explanation: The speed of light in glass is v = c/n = 3.0 x 10^8 divided by 1.50 = 2.0 x 10^8 m s-1. The thickness 0.9 cm must be converted to 9.0 x 10-3 m. Time is distance over speed, so t = 9.0 x 10-3 divided by 2.0 x 10^8 = 4.5 x 10-11 s. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When an object is placed between the principal focus and the optical center of a convex lens, it could be used as a?
questions.explanation: When an object is placed between the optical centre and principal focus of a convex lens, the lens forms a virtual, erect, magnified image on the same side as the object. That is exactly how a simple microscope or magnifying glass operates. A projector requires a real image and therefore uses a different object position. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The production of pure spectrum could easily be achieved using a?
options: triangular prism with two convex lens
triangular prism with two concave lenses
questions.explanation: A pure spectrum is obtained most effectively by first rendering the incident light parallel with one convex lens, dispersing it through a triangular prism, and then focusing the separated colours with a second convex lens. A prism alone gives dispersion but not the cleanest pure spectrum arrangement. Concave lenses are unsuitable here. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A charge 50 µc has electric field strength of 360 NC-1 at a certain point. The electric field strength due to another charge 120 µc kept at the same distance apart and in the same medium is?
questions.explanation: At a fixed distance in the same medium, electric field strength due to a point charge is directly proportional to the charge. So E2/E1 = Q2/Q1. Using E1 = 360 N C-1, Q1 = 50 microcoulombs, and Q2 = 120 microcoulombs gives E2 = 360 x 120/50 = 864 N C-1. The unit and proportional reasoning both fit option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A conductor has a diameter of 1.00 mm and length 2.00m. if the resistance of the material is 0.1Ω, its resistivity is?
questions.explanation: Resistivity is rho = RA/L. The conductor radius is half the diameter, so r = 0.50 mm = 5.0 x 10-4 m. Its cross-sectional area is A = pi r^2 about 7.85 x 10-7 m^2. Hence rho = 0.1 x 7.85 x 10-7 divided by 2.00 about 3.93 x 10-8 ohm metre. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
The energy E of a photon and its wavelength are related by Eλ = X. the numerical value of X is?

[h = 6.63 x 10\(^{-34}\)js, c = 3 x 10\(^8\) ms\(^{-1}\)]
questions.explanation: For a photon, E = hf and f = c divided by wavelength, so E = hc divided by wavelength. Multiplying by wavelength gives E times wavelength = hc. Substituting h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s and c = 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 gives X = 1.989 x 10^-25 J m, which rounds to 1.99 x 10^-25. That matches option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The bond that forms a semiconductor is?
questions.explanation: In elemental semiconductors such as silicon and germanium, neighbouring atoms share valence electrons to complete their outer shells. This shared-electron arrangement is covalent bonding. Ionic or electrovalent bonding involves electron transfer, while metallic bonding involves a sea of mobile electrons typical of metals. Therefore the bond forming the semiconductor crystal is covalent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Silicon doped with aluminum and germanium doped with arsenic become?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is trivalent, so when it dopes silicon it creates holes and produces p-type material. Arsenic is pentavalent, so when it dopes germanium it donates extra electrons and produces n-type material. The semiconductor types therefore occur in the order p-type then n-type. This matches option 0 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Force (N)

II.Torque (Nm)

III. Current (A)

IV. Power (W)

Which of the above are the correct S. I: units of the quantities indicated?
options: I, II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: Each quantity is paired with its standard SI unit correctly: force with newton, torque with newton metre, current with ampere, and power with watt. None of the listed unit pairings is wrong. Therefore all four statements are correct, making the appropriate option I, II, III and IV only. The notation used is consistent with SI practice.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: A vector must have both magnitude and a definite direction. Acceleration, displacement, and weight all possess direction and are vector quantities. Altitude is simply a height above a reference level and is treated here as a scalar quantity. It does not by itself function as a vector in the way the others do. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a wheel 1.2 m in diameter rotates at one revolution per second, calculate the velocity of the wheel.
questions.explanation: A point on the rim moves one circumference in one second because the wheel makes one revolution per second. The circumference is pi d = pi x 1.2 m, so the linear speed is 1.2 pi m s-1 about 3.77 m s-1. This is the tangential speed of the wheel rim. Therefore the correct option is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the frequency of vibration if the balance wheel of a wrist watch makes 90 revolutions in 25 s?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of cycles or revolutions completed per second. The balance wheel makes 90 revolutions in 25 s, so f = 90/25 = 3.6 s-1. Since 1 s-1 is 1 hertz, the frequency is 3.60 Hz. The calculation is direct and matches option 3 without any ambiguity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a body mass 5kg is thrown vertically upwards with velocity u,at what height will the potential energy equal to the kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: The body starts with total mechanical energy equal to 1/2 m u^2. At the height where potential energy equals kinetic energy, each must be half of the total energy, so mgh = 1/4 m u^2. Cancelling mass and solving for h gives h = u^2/4g. The result is independent of the given 5 kg mass. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Counting of currency notes with moist fingers is based on the principles of?
questions.explanation: Counting notes with moist fingers depends on adhesion, the attraction between unlike materials. A thin film of moisture helps the skin adhere slightly to the paper surface, so one note can be separated more easily from the next. Diffusion is mixing of particles, cohesion is attraction between like molecules, and viscosity concerns fluid flow. The defensible choice is adhesion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A motorcycle of mass 100kg moves round in a circle of radius 10m with a velocity of 5 ms\(^{-1}\). find the coefficient of friction between the road and the tyres.
questions.explanation: For motion in a horizontal circle, friction supplies the centripetal force. Thus mu mg = mv squared over r, so mu = v squared over rg. Substituting v = 5 m s minus 1, r = 10 m, and g about 10 m s minus 2 gives mu = 25 over 100 = 0.25. The mass cancels, and the result is dimensionless, as required for a coefficient of friction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A spring of force constant 500 Nm\(^{-1}\) is compressed such that its length shortens by 5cm. The energy stored in the spring is?
questions.explanation: Elastic potential energy stored in a compressed spring is one half kx squared. Here k = 500 N per m and the compression is 5 cm, which must be converted to 0.05 m. Therefore energy = 0.5 times 500 times 0.05 squared = 250 times 0.0025 = 0.625 J. The numerical value, unit, and physical interpretation are all consistent with option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the hare's apparatus, water rises to a height of 26.5 cm in one limb. if a liquid rises to a height of 20.4 cm in the other limb, what is the relative density of the liquid?
questions.explanation: In Hare’s apparatus, the same suction produces equal pressure differences in both limbs, so density times height is the same for the two liquids. Hence relative density of the unknown liquid equals height of water column divided by height of liquid column. This gives 26.5 over 20.4 = 1.299, which rounds to 1.3. A denser liquid rising to a smaller height is physically sensible.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When cold water is poured on a can containing hot water, the can collapses because the?
options: steam condeses and occupies the partial vacuum in the can
external air pressure counter balances the pressure within the can
steam expands to occupy the vacuum remaining in the can
external pressure becomes greater than the pressure within the can.
questions.explanation: When cold water is poured on the can, steam inside condenses to liquid water. Because condensation greatly reduces the amount of gas inside, the internal pressure falls sharply. Atmospheric pressure outside then exceeds the pressure within the can and crushes it inward. Option 3 states this directly. Options mentioning steam occupying a vacuum are physically incorrect, since condensation reduces, not increases, the internal gas pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An empty density bottle weighs 2 N. if it weighs 5 N when filled with water and 4 N when filled with olive oil, the relative density of olive oil is?
questions.explanation: Relative density is the weight of a given volume of the liquid divided by the weight of an equal volume of water. The bottle itself must first be excluded. Water alone weighs 5 minus 2 = 3 N, and olive oil alone weighs 4 minus 2 = 2 N. So relative density = 2 over 3. That matches option 1 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The thermometric properties of a thermocouple is the change in?
questions.explanation: A thermocouple uses the Seebeck effect. When two dissimilar metals form junctions at different temperatures, an electromotive force is generated, and that e.m.f. varies with temperature. This varying e.m.f. is the thermometric property used to measure temperature. Equivalent resistance, colour, and pressure are the relevant properties of other devices, not of a thermocouple. Therefore the correct choice is electromotive force.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: During summer, the balance wheel of a clock expands.what effect does this have on the accuracy of the clock?
options: the accuracy of the clock is not affected
questions.explanation: Heating the balance wheel makes it expand, increasing its radius and therefore its moment of inertia. A larger moment of inertia makes the oscillation period longer, so each beat takes more time than before. The clock therefore runs slow and loses time. The correct option is the one stating that the clock loses time; the draft idea is right though the original wording contains a spelling error.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A sealed flask contains 600cm3 of air at 27°C and is heated to 35°C at constant pressure. The new volume is?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, Charles’s law applies: volume is proportional to absolute temperature. The initial temperature is 27 plus 273 = 300 K and the final temperature is 35 plus 273 = 308 K. Therefore V2 = 600 times 308 over 300 = 616 cm cubed. The increase is small but positive, which is consistent with heating a gas at constant pressure.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A block of aluminum is heated electrically by a 25 W heater. if the temperature rises by 10°C in 5 minutes, the heat capacity of the aluminum is?
questions.explanation: The heater supplies energy Q = Pt. With power 25 W and time 5 minutes = 300 s, the heat supplied is 25 times 300 = 7500 J. Heat capacity C is Q divided by temperature rise, so C = 7500 over 10 = 750 J per K. The question asks for total heat capacity, not specific heat capacity, so no mass term is required.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the partial pressure of water vapour at 27°C is 18 mm Hg and the saturated vapour pressure of the atmosphere at the same temperature is 24 mm Hg, the relative humidity at this temperature is?
questions.explanation: Relative humidity is defined as actual vapour pressure divided by saturated vapour pressure at the same temperature, multiplied by 100 percent. Using the given values, 18 over 24 times 100 gives 75 percent. Since the actual vapour pressure is below the saturated value, the humidity must be below 100 percent. The correct option is therefore 75 percent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a good thermos flask, heat loss is reduced through the following features EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: A good thermos flask reduces heat transfer by features such as silvered walls, an insulating cork, and a cork lid. These limit radiation, conduction, and convection. A lens surface is not a standard heat-conserving feature of a thermos flask and does not explain its insulating action. Since the question asks for the exception, option 0 is the defensible answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Given the progressive wave equation y = 5 sin (2000 πt - 0.4x), calculate wave length
questions.explanation: A progressive wave can be written as y = A sin of omega t minus kx, where k is the wave number. Comparing with the given equation shows k = 0.4 rad per m. Wavelength lambda equals 2 pi over k, so lambda = 2 pi over 0.4 = 5 pi m, approximately 15.7 m. Amplitude 5 does not affect wavelength.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The fundamental property of a propagating wave which depends only on the source and not the medium of propagation is the?
questions.explanation: The frequency of a wave is fixed by the source that produces the oscillation. When a wave passes into another medium, its speed and wavelength may change to suit the new medium, but the source continues vibrating at the same rate, so frequency remains unchanged. Harmonics are not the basic propagation property being asked here. Therefore the correct answer is frequency.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Total internal reflection of light.

II. Conservation of light energy.

III. Relative motion of the earth, sun and moon.

IV. Rectilinear propagation of light.

which of the above is a phenomenon of total solar eclipse?
questions.explanation: A total solar eclipse occurs because of the relative positions and motion of the Sun, Moon, and Earth, and because light travels in straight lines so the Moon casts a shadow on Earth. Total internal reflection is irrelevant, and conservation of light energy is not the operative phenomenon. Therefore only statements III and IV apply, making option 3 correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object of height 4cm is placed in front of a cuboid pinhole camera of size 6 cm. if the image formed is 2 cm high, how far is the object from the pinhole?
questions.explanation: In a pinhole camera, the object and image heights are proportional to their distances from the pinhole because of similar triangles. Thus image height over object height equals camera length over object distance. Substituting 2 over 4 = 6 over u gives u = 12 cm. The smaller image also supports the object being farther away than the camera length. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object of heights 5 cm is placed at 20 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. the image height is?
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, use 1 over f = 1 over u plus 1 over v with the school sign convention based on magnitudes here. With f = 10 cm and u = 20 cm, 1 over v = 1 over 10 minus 1 over 20 = 1 over 20, so v = 20 cm. Magnification is v over u = 1, hence image height equals object height. The image height is therefore 5 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Convex mirror are used as driving mirrors because images formed are?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms an image that is virtual, upright, and smaller than the object for any real object placed in front of it. This diminished image gives a wider field of view, which is why convex mirrors are used as driving mirrors. A real image is not produced by a convex mirror under ordinary use. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object placed at the bottom of a well full of clear water appears closer to the surface due to?
questions.explanation: The bottom of a water-filled well appears raised because light from the object bends when it passes from water into air. The rays refract away from the normal and the eye traces them backward to an apparent point nearer the surface. That makes the depth look smaller than the real depth. Reflection, diffraction, and polarization do not produce this apparent shallowness. Therefore the answer is refraction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In the microscope, the eyepiece lens merely acts as?
questions.explanation: In a compound microscope, the objective first forms a real, enlarged intermediate image of the specimen. The eyepiece then acts like a simple magnifying glass, enlarging the appearance of that intermediate image for the observer. Its essential role is therefore magnification, not inversion, refinement, or diminution. Hence the eyepiece lens merely acts as a magnifier, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Short sightedness can be corrected by what type of lens?
questions.explanation: Short sightedness, or myopia, means distant objects are focused in front of the retina. A concave lens diverges incoming rays before they enter the eye, allowing the eye lens to focus them properly on the retina. A convex or converging lens would move the focus in the wrong direction. Therefore the correcting lens is a concave lens, option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A short chain is sometimes attached to the back of a petrol tanker to?
options: ensure the balancing of the tanker
conduct excess charges to the earth
questions.explanation: As a petrol tanker moves, friction with air and road can build up static electric charge on the metal body. A trailing chain touches the ground and provides a conducting path to Earth, allowing the charge to leak away safely. This reduces the chance of a spark that could ignite petrol vapour. Therefore the chain is attached to conduct excess charges to the earth.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric generator has e.m.f. of 240 V and an internal resistance of 1Ω if the current supplied by the generator is 20A when the terminal voltage is 220 V, find the ratio of the power supplied to the power dissipated?
questions.explanation: The useful power supplied to the external circuit is terminal voltage times current: 220 times 20 = 4400 W. The internal power loss in the generator is I squared r = 20 squared times 1 = 400 W. Therefore the ratio of power supplied to power dissipated is 4400 to 400, which simplifies to 11 to 1. The emf value is consistent since 240 minus 220 equals 20 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The d.c generator has essentially the same components as the a.c generator except the presence of?
questions.explanation: Both a.c. and d.c. generators have an armature and carbon brushes. The essential difference is the current-collecting arrangement. A d.c. generator uses a split-ring commutator, which reverses the connection each half turn so that the external current remains in one direction. An a.c. generator instead uses slip rings. Therefore the distinguishing component for the d.c. generator is the split ring.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A step-down transformer has a power output of 50 W and efficiency of 80%. if the mains supply voltage is 200 v, calculate the primary current of the transformer.
questions.explanation: Efficiency equals output power divided by input power. With output power 50 W and efficiency 0.80, the input power is 50 over 0.80 = 62.5 W. The mains voltage is the primary voltage, 200 V, so primary current is input power divided by primary voltage: 62.5 over 200 = 0.3125 A. Rounded appropriately, this is 0.31 A, which matches option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
Caesium has a work function of 3 x 10\(^{-19}\)J. The maximum energy of liberated electrons when it is illuminated by light of frequency 6.7 x 10\(^{14}\)

HZ is? [h = 6.6 x 10\(^{-34}\)Js]
questions.explanation: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by hf minus the work function. Photon energy is 6.6 times 10 to the minus 34 multiplied by 6.7 times 10 to the 14, which equals 4.422 times 10 to the minus 19 J. Subtracting the work function 3.0 times 10 to the minus 19 J gives 1.422 times 10 to the minus 19 J. So option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: zener diode is used for?
questions.explanation: A zener diode is designed to operate in reverse breakdown, where the voltage across it remains nearly constant over a useful current range. Because of this property, it is used to stabilize or regulate voltage in circuits. It is not a device for current amplification, power amplification, or general energy conversion. Therefore the correct answer is voltage regulation, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a pure semiconductor is heated, its resistance?
questions.explanation: In a pure semiconductor, heating generates more electron-hole pairs. The increased number of charge carriers raises the conductivity, so the electrical resistance falls as temperature rises. This behavior is opposite to that of most metallic conductors, whose resistance usually increases when heated. Therefore the correct choice is that the resistance decreases, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. for current amplification.

II. for voltage stabilization.

III. for power amplification.

IV. as a switch.

which of the above are the uses of transistor?
questions.explanation: A transistor is commonly used for current amplification, power amplification, and as an electronic switch. In elementary physics, voltage stabilization is classically assigned to the zener diode rather than to the transistor itself as a primary device function. Therefore statement II should not be included. The defensible set is I, III, and IV only, corresponding to option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Diameter of a small ball bearing.

II. Thickness of a pieces of paper.

III. Diameter of a measuring cylinder.

IV. Length of a piece of wire.

Which of the above can be measured using a micrometer screw gauge?
questions.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge is used for small external dimensions with high precision, typically over a limited range such as 0 to 25 mm. It can measure the diameter of a small ball bearing and the thickness of paper or a small stack of papers. It is not suitable for the full length of a wire, and a measuring cylinder’s diameter is generally too large for its range. Therefore only I and II are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A bullet fired vertically upward from a gun held 2.0 m above the ground reaches its maximum height in 4.0s. calculate its initial velocity.

[g = 10ms\(^-2\)]
questions.explanation: At the highest point of its motion, the bullet’s vertical velocity is zero. Using v = u minus gt, set v = 0, g = 10 m s minus 2, and t = 4 s. Then u = gt = 40 m s minus 1. The initial height of 2.0 m above the ground does not affect the time taken to reach maximum height. Thus the correct option is 40 m s minus 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
If a cage containing a truck of coal weighing 750 kg is raised to a height of 90 m in a minute, what is the total power expended?

[g = 10 m\s\(^2\)]
questions.explanation: Power expended in raising a load is work done against gravity per unit time. The work is mgh = 750 times 10 times 90 = 675000 J. Dividing by 60 s gives 11250 W, which is 11.25 kW. The printed value of g in the question appears malformed, but using the stated numerical value 10 gives a clear and standard result. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a heavy barrel is rolled up a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. its velocity ratio will be?
questions.explanation: For an inclined plane, the velocity ratio is the distance moved by the effort divided by the vertical distance gained by the load. Geometrically this equals the length of the plane over its height, which is 1 over sine theta. With theta = 30 degrees, sine 30 degrees = 0.5, so the velocity ratio is 2. The barrel being rolled does not alter this geometric result.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a load of mass 10N stretched a cord by 1.2cm, what is the total work done?
questions.explanation: If the cord obeys Hooke’s law, the stretching force increases from zero to 10 N as extension grows to 1.2 cm. The work done is therefore one half times final force times extension. Converting 1.2 cm to 0.012 m gives W = 0.5 times 10 times 0.012 = 0.06 J, which is 6.0 times 10 to the minus 2 J. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A plastic sphere floats in water with 50% of its volume submerged. if it floats in glycerine with 40% of its volume submerged,the density of the glycerine is?
questions.explanation: For a floating body, weight equals upthrust, so the fraction submerged equals density of the body divided by density of the liquid. In water, 0.50 = density of sphere over 1000, giving density of sphere = 500 kg per m cubed. In glycerine, 0.40 = 500 over density of glycerine, so density of glycerine = 1250 kg per m cubed. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The thermometer whose reading is indicated by a change in color of its thermometric property is the?
questions.explanation: An optical pyrometer measures temperature by comparing the colour or brightness of radiation from a hot object. Its thermometric property is therefore a change in emitted radiation appearance, often described at this level as colour. A thermocouple uses e.m.f., a platinum resistance thermometer uses resistance, and a bimetallic strip uses unequal expansion. Hence the correct thermometer is the optical pyrometer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: At 4°c, the volume of a fixed mass of water is?
questions.explanation: Water shows anomalous expansion. As it is cooled from higher temperatures down to 4 degrees Celsius, it contracts and its density increases. At 4 degrees Celsius the density is maximum. For a fixed mass, maximum density means minimum volume. If cooled below 4 degrees Celsius, water expands again. Therefore the volume of a fixed mass of water at 4 degrees Celsius is minimum.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric heater rated 220V, 1000 W is immersed into a bucket full of water. Calculate the mass of water if the temperature changes from 30°c to 100°c and the current flows for 300seconds. [specific heat capacity of water = 4200 jkg-1 K-1]
questions.explanation: Electrical energy delivered by the heater is Pt = 1000 times 300 = 300000 J. Assuming all of this heats the water, Q = mc delta T, with delta T = 100 minus 30 = 70 K and c = 4200 J per kg per K. So m = 300000 over 4200 times 70 = about 1.02 kg. The correct option is therefore 1.02 kg.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the pressure of the vapor on top of an enclosed liquid is equal to the atmospheric pressure, what will be the temperature of the liquid enclosed?
questions.explanation: A liquid boils when its vapour pressure becomes equal to the external pressure acting on its surface. If the vapour pressure above the enclosed liquid equals atmospheric pressure, then the liquid is at the temperature where boiling occurs under that atmospheric pressure. Therefore the temperature is the boiling point, not room temperature, freezing point, or a generic standard temperature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A heating coil rated 1000 W is used to boil off completely 2 kg of boiling water. The time required to boil the water is?

[Special latent heat of Vaporization of water = 2.3 x 10\(^6\) Jkg-1]
questions.explanation: Since the water is already boiling, no sensible heating is needed; only latent heat of vaporization is required. The energy needed is Q = mL = 2 times 2.3 times 10 to the 6 = 4.6 times 10 to the 6 J. With heater power 1000 W, time = Q over P = 4.6 times 10 to the 6 over 1000 = 4.6 times 10 to the 3 s. Option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: It is observed that water will wet a clean glass because the?
options: cohesion of water to glass is stronger than the cohesion of water molecules
adhesion of water molecules is weaker than the cohesion of water to glass
cohesion of water to glass is weaker than the cohesion of water molecules
adhesion of water molecules is stronger than the cohesion of water molecules
questions.explanation: A liquid wets a surface when the adhesive attraction between the liquid and the surface is greater than the cohesive attraction among the liquid molecules themselves. For clean glass and water, attraction to the glass is stronger, so water spreads over the surface instead of forming isolated droplets. Although the option wording is imperfect, option 3 expresses the correct comparison between adhesion and cohesion.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A man standing 2 m from a charcoal fire is warmed mainly by?
questions.explanation: At a distance of about 2 m from a charcoal fire, the dominant heat transfer to a person is thermal radiation. Conduction requires direct contact, which is absent. Convection mainly carries heated air upward rather than directly across to the person. Refraction is unrelated to heat transfer. Therefore the main warming mechanism is radiation, making option 1 correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Musical instruments playing the same note can be distinguished from one another owing to the differences in their?
questions.explanation: If different instruments play the same note, they have the same frequency, so their pitch is the same. They are distinguished by differences in waveform and overtone content, which give different timbre or tone colour. In school physics this property is called quality. Intensity and loudness concern strength of sound, not identity of instruments playing the same note. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
I. Moon.

II. Sun.

III.street light.

IV. stars.

Which of these are natural sources of light?
questions.explanation: A natural source of light must emit its own light and must not be man-made. The Sun and the stars satisfy this condition. The Moon does not emit its own visible light; it reflects sunlight, so it is not a light source in this classification. A street light is artificial. Therefore the natural sources listed are II and IV only, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object is placed 5 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. if the focal length of the mirror is 10 cm. what is the image distance?
options: 10 cm in front of the mirror.
5 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, an object placed inside the focal length forms a virtual image behind the mirror. Using the mirror equation with magnitudes, 1 over f = 1 over u plus 1 over v and substituting f = 10 cm, u = 5 cm gives 1 over v = 1 over 10 minus 1 over 5 = minus 1 over 10. Hence v = minus 10 cm, meaning 10 cm behind the mirror.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Calculate the position of an object placed in front of a convex mirror having focal length of 12 cm such that an image is formed 6 cm away from the mirror
questions.explanation: Use the mirror formula with the Cartesian sign convention: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. For a convex mirror, f = -12 cm. The image is virtual and 6 cm behind the mirror, so v = +6 cm. Then 1/u = -1/12 - 1/6 = -1/4, giving u = -4 cm. The negative sign means the object is in front of the mirror, so its distance is 4.0 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the refractive index of crown glass is 1.51, its critical angle is?
questions.explanation: For the critical angle at a glass to air boundary, sin C = 1/n. With refractive index n = 1.51, sin C = 1/1.51 = 0.6623. Taking the inverse sine gives C about 41.5 degrees. This is the limiting angle in the denser medium for which the refracted ray just grazes the boundary. Therefore the correct option is 41.5 degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When light passes through two media x and y of refraction indices 1.51 and 1.33 respectively, the speed of light in
options: x is same as in y
x and y is same as in vacuum
x is higher than in y
y is higher than in x
questions.explanation: The refractive index relation is n = c/v, so v = c/n. Light therefore travels more slowly in the medium with larger refractive index. Medium x has n = 1.51 while medium y has n = 1.33. Since 1.33 is smaller than 1.51, the speed of light is greater in y than in x. Hence the correct choice is that y is higher than x.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The ability of the human eye to focus object on the retina is referred to as the power of?
questions.explanation: The correct term is accommodation. This is the ability of the eye lens, controlled by the ciliary muscles, to change its focal length so that images of objects at different distances are focused sharply on the retina. Interference, diffraction, and superposition are wave effects and do not describe the focusing action of the eye. Therefore accommodation is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If negative charges are induced on an electroscope and a positively charged rod is brought near the cap of the electroscope, the leaves will?
questions.explanation: A negatively charged electroscope has excess electrons on the leaves, so they diverge because like charges repel. When a positively charged rod is brought near the cap, electrons in the electroscope are attracted upward toward the cap. This reduces the negative charge on the leaves and weakens their repulsion. The leaves therefore move closer together. Hence the correct option is that they close up.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric lamp marked 240v, 60 W is left to operate for an hour. How much energy is generated by the filament?
questions.explanation: Electrical energy produced is given by E = Pt. The lamp power is 60 W, meaning 60 joules per second, and the time is 1 hour = 3600 s. So E = 60 x 3600 = 216000 J = 2.16 x 10^5 J. The voltage marking is irrelevant once the power is already provided. Therefore the correct answer is 2.16 x 10^5 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A band of 500 rectangular loops of wire of area 20 cm by 20 cm, encloses a region of magnetic field which charges from 1.0T to 0.4T within 5 seconds, calculate the induced e.m.f.
questions.explanation: By Faraday's law, induced e.m.f. = N delta Phi divided by time = N A delta B divided by t, assuming the field is normal to the coil. Here N = 500 and A = 20 cm x 20 cm = 0.20 m x 0.20 m = 0.04 m squared. The field changes from 1.0 T to 0.4 T, so delta B = 0.6 T in 5 s. Thus e.m.f. = 500 x 0.04 x 0.6 divided by 5 = 2.40 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Cancerous cells can be destroyed by?
questions.explanation: Cancerous cells are commonly destroyed by ionizing radiation in radiotherapy. X-rays are sufficiently penetrating and ionizing to damage and kill rapidly dividing cells within the body. Ultraviolet radiation does not penetrate deeply enough for this standard use, infrared mainly produces heating, and alpha particles have very low penetration despite strong ionization. Therefore the correct answer is x-rays.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the decay constant of a radioactive substance is 0.231s-\(^1\), the half-life is?
questions.explanation: The half-life is related to decay constant by T half = 0.693 divided by lambda. Given lambda = 0.231 per second, T half = 0.693 divided by 0.231 = 3.00 s. The unit is seconds because the decay constant is measured in inverse seconds. Therefore the substance takes 3.00 s for half of its nuclei to decay, so option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text:
A piece of radioactive material contains 10\(^{20}\) atoms.

If the half life of the material is 20 seconds, the number of disintegration in the first second is?
questions.explanation: The activity in the first second is approximately A = lambda N, where lambda = 0.693 divided by T half. With T half = 20 s, lambda = 0.693 divided by 20 = 0.03465 per second. For N = 10^20 atoms, A = 0.03465 x 10^20 = 3.465 x 10^18 disintegrations per second. In the first second this is about 3.47 x 10^18 disintegrations, matching option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Thermionic emission is the process whereby?
questions.explanation: Thermionic emission is the emission of electrons from a metal surface when it is heated sufficiently. Heating gives some electrons enough energy to overcome the surface potential barrier and escape. It does not refer to the production of beta rays, x-rays, or holes. Therefore the correct description is that electrons leave a hot element. That corresponds to option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following can conduct electricity owing to the presence of free mobile electrons?
questions.explanation: Metals conduct electricity because they possess many free mobile electrons that drift under an applied electric field. Copper is a metal and therefore conducts by this mechanism very effectively. Germanium and silicon are semiconductors, whose conduction is not characterized in this simple metallic way, and grapefruit is not a metallic conductor. Hence the correct answer is copper.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a pentavalent impurity is added to a pure semiconductor, it becomes?
questions.explanation: A pentavalent impurity has five valence electrons.
