questions.text: A far sighted person cannot see objects that are less than 100cm away. If this person wants to read a book at 25cm, what type and focal length of lens does he need?
questions.explanation: A far-sighted person has a near point at 100 cm, so a reading lens must make a book at 25 cm appear as a virtual image at 100 cm. Using the thin lens formula with u = -25 cm and v = -100 cm gives 1/f = 1/25 - 1/100 = 3/100. Thus f about 33.3 cm, and the lens must be converging. Option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a yellow card is observed through a blue glass, the card would appear.
questions.explanation: A yellow object reflects mainly red and green light and absorbs blue. A blue glass transmits blue light but absorbs most red and green light. Since the yellow card sends essentially no blue light through the filter, very little or no light reaches the eye. The card therefore appears black. Hence option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Dispersion of light by a glass prism is due to the
options: different speeds of the various colours in glass
questions.explanation: Dispersion by a prism occurs because different colours have different refractive indices in glass. Equivalently, they travel at different speeds in the glass and are refracted by different amounts. This separation produces the spectrum. The effect is not caused by glass defects, the glass having colours of its own, or density alone. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following pairs is NOT part of the electromagnetic spectrum? i. Radio waves. ii. Beta rays. iii. Gamma rays. iv. Alpha rays
questions.explanation: Radio waves and gamma rays are electromagnetic waves. Beta rays are streams of electrons or positrons, and alpha rays are helium nuclei, so both are particle radiations rather than members of the electromagnetic spectrum. Therefore the pair that is not part of the electromagnetic spectrum is ii and iv. This matches option 3, despite the duplicated wording in option 0.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two insulated charged spheres of different sizes and carrying opposite charges are connected together by a metallic conductor. Current will flow from one sphere to the other until both sphere
options: carry the same magnitude and sign of charge
questions.explanation: When two charged conducting spheres are connected by a metallic conductor, charge flows because their electric potentials differ. The flow continues until electrostatic equilibrium is reached, and equilibrium requires equal potential, not equal charge or equal size. Spheres of different radii can end with different charges while still sharing the same potential. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a number of identical small magnets are arranged in a line, the strength of the resultant magnet
options: ia largest when they are arranged end to end
is greatest when they are arrangedparallel with like poles adjacent to each other
depends only on the number of magnets provided they arev parallel
is greater when the magnets are arranged on a wooden surface than on a metaln surface
questions.explanation: Identical bar magnets give the strongest resultant when placed end to end with unlike poles touching, so their magnetic moments reinforce along the same line and form a longer effective magnet. Placing like poles adjacent in parallel is not the strongest arrangement, and the supporting surface material is irrelevant here. Therefore option 0 is the correct choice despite typographical errors in the text.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A bar magnet is most effectively demagnetized by
options: placing it in a N - S position and hitting it with a hammer
subjecting it to an electric current from a battery
bringing its north pole in contact with the north pole of a very strong magnet
questions.explanation: Heating a magnet strongly disturbs the alignment of its magnetic domains through thermal agitation, reducing or destroying its magnetization. Hammering can demagnetize in some cases, especially in the Earth's field, but it is less definitive than heating in the context of the given options. Therefore the most effective listed method is heating the magnet, which is option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The resistance of a 5m uniform wire of cross-sectional area 0.2 x 10-6m2 is 0.425. What is the resistivity of the material of the wire?
questions.explanation: Resistivity is found from R = rho L/A, so rho = RA/L. With R = 0.425 ohm, A = 0.2 x 10^-6 square metres, and L = 5 m, rho = 0.425 x 0.2 x 10^-6 divided by 5 = 0.017 x 10^-6 = 1.7 x 10^-8 ohm metre. This matches option 3 exactly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Three resistors, with substances 250\(\Omega\), 500\(\Omega\) and 1k\(\Omega\) are connected in series. A 6V battery is connected to either end of the combination. Calculate the pot3ential difference between the end of the 250\(\Omega\) resistor.
questions.explanation: In series, the same current flows through all three resistors. The total resistance is 250 + 500 + 1000 = 1750 ohms. Using Ohm’s law, the current is I = 6/1750 A, about 3.43 x 10^-3 A. The p.d. across the 250 ohm resistor is V = IR = (6/1750) x 250 = 0.857 V, which rounds to 0.86 V. That matches option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A calibrated potentiometer is used to measure the e.m.f. of a cell because the
options: internal resistance of a cell is small compared with that of the potentiometer
potentiometer takes no current from the cell
resistance of the potentiometer is less than that of a voltmeter
questions.explanation: A potentiometer measures e.m.f. by a null method. At balance, no current is drawn from the cell under test, so there is no voltage drop across its internal resistance. The measured value is therefore the true e.m.f. rather than a loaded terminal p.d. This is the essential reason for using a potentiometer, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The electrochemical equivalent of silver is 0.0012gC-1. If 36.0g of silver is to be deposited by electrolysis on a surface by passing a steady current for 5.0mins, the current must be
questions.explanation: For electrolysis, deposited mass is m = ZIt. Hence I = m/(Zt). Using m = 36.0 g, Z = 0.0012 g per coulomb, and t = 5.0 minutes = 300 s gives I = 36.0 divided by 0.0012 x 300 = 36.0/0.36 = 100 A. Therefore the required steady current is 100 A, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a radiation strikes a metal surface, electrons may be ejected from the metal. The maximum kinetic energy which may be acquired by an ejected electron depend on the
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is given by Kmax = hf minus the work function. Since frequency and wavelength are inversely related, the maximum kinetic energy depends on the wavelength of the incident radiation. Intensity mainly changes the number of emitted electrons, not their maximum kinetic energy. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE of the particles emitted in radioactive disintegration?
options: the beta particle is the helium nucleus H
the alpha particle is lighter than the beta particle
the alpha particle is deflected more than the beta particle in a magnetic field
the beta particle is deflected more than the alpha particle in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: A beta particle is an electron or positron, while an alpha particle is a helium nucleus. In a magnetic field, deflection depends on charge-to-mass ratio. Because beta particles have much smaller mass, their charge-to-mass ratio is far larger than that of alpha particles, so they bend more strongly. Therefore the true statement is that the beta particle is deflected more than the alpha particle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Eight alpha decays and six beta decays are necessary before an atom of 2 \(^{238}_{92}U\) achieves stability. The final product in the chain has an atomic number of
questions.explanation: Each alpha decay lowers the atomic number by 2, while each beta minus decay raises it by 1. Starting from uranium with atomic number 92, eight alpha decays reduce it by 16 to 76. Six beta decays then increase it by 6 to 82. So the final stable product has atomic number 82, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following are the correct SI units of the quantities indicated? i.N(Force) II. N/m (Torque) iii. watt(Power) iv. kgms-2(Momentum)
questions.explanation: Force has SI unit newton, so item i is correct. Torque should have unit newton metre, not newton per metre, so item ii is wrong. Power is measured in watt, so item iii is correct. Momentum should be kilogram metre per second, not kilogram metre per second squared, so item iv is wrong. Therefore only i and iii are correct, giving option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A lorry travels 10km northwards, 4km eastwards, 6km southwards, 4km westwards to arrive at a point T. What is the total displacement?
questions.explanation: Treat each part of the journey as a displacement vector. The 4 km eastward motion and the 4 km westward motion cancel completely, leaving no net east-west displacement. Vertically, 10 km north minus 6 km south leaves 4 km north. The attached diagram is consistent with this vector cancellation. Therefore the total displacement is 4 km north, option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two forces whose resultant is 100N, are at right angle to each other. If one of them makes an angle 30o with the resultant, determine its magnitude.
questions.explanation: The two perpendicular forces and their resultant form a right triangle. If one force makes 30 degrees with the resultant, that force is adjacent to the 30 degree angle, while the resultant is the hypotenuse. Hence its magnitude is F = R cos 30 degrees = 100 x 0.866 = 86.6 N. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following quantities are scalars? i. Electrical potential ii. Torque iii. Momentum iv. Kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Electrical potential is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude only. Torque has direction and is treated as a vector, and momentum is also a vector since it depends on direction of motion. Kinetic energy is scalar. Therefore the scalar quantities listed are i and iv only, which corresponds to option 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When taking a penalty kick, a footballer applies a force of 30.0N for a period of 0.05s. if the mass of the ball is 0.075kg, calculate the speed with which the ball moves off.
questions.explanation: Impulse equals change in momentum. The ball starts from rest, so Ft = mv. Using F = 30.0 N and t = 0.05 s gives impulse 30.0 x 0.05 = 1.5 N s. Therefore v = 1.5/0.075 = 20.0 m/s. The speed with which the ball moves off is 20.00 m/s, so option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A particle starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration of 0.5ms\(^{-2}\). The distance covered by the particle in 10s is?
questions.explanation: The particle starts from rest, so initial velocity u = 0. For constant acceleration, distance is s = ut + 1/2 at squared. Substituting a = 0.5 m/s squared and t = 10 s gives s = 0 + 1/2 x 0.5 x 10 squared = 0.25 x 100 = 25 m. Thus the distance covered is 25.0 m, which is option 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 20-toothed gear wheel drives a 60-toothed one. If the angular speed of the smaller wheel is 120 rev s-1, the angular speed of the larger wheel is
questions.explanation: For meshing gears, the angular speed is inversely proportional to the number of teeth because the tangential speeds at contact are equal. Thus N1 omega1 = N2 omega2. With 20 teeth and 120 rev/s for the smaller gear, and 60 teeth for the larger gear, omega2 = 20 x 120 divided by 60 = 40 rev/s. Therefore option 1 is correct, not the supplied answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A force, 10N, drags a mass 10kg on a horizontal table with an acceleration of 0.2ms. If the acceleration due to gravity is 10ms-1, the coefficient of friction between the moving mass and the table is
questions.explanation: The net horizontal force is applied force minus friction. So 10 - friction = ma = 10 x 0.2 = 2 N, giving friction = 8 N. On a horizontal table, the normal reaction is mg = 10 x 10 = 100 N. Therefore the coefficient of friction is mu = 8/100 = 0.08. Option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body whose mass is 2kg and has a volume of 500cm3 just floats when completely immersed in a liquid. Calculate the density of the liquid
questions.explanation: If the body just floats when completely immersed, its density equals the density of the liquid. The body's density is mass divided by volume. Convert 500 cubic centimetres to 5 x 10^-4 cubic metres. Then density = 2 divided by 5 x 10^-4 = 4.0 x 10^3 kg/m^3. Therefore the liquid density is 4.0 x 10^3 kg/m^3, which is option 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The product PV where P is pressure and V is volume has the same unit as
questions.explanation: Pressure has unit pascal, which is newton per square metre, and volume has unit cubic metre. Multiplying gives newton metre. A newton metre is a joule, the unit of work or energy. Force alone is measured in newtons, power in joules per second, and acceleration in metres per second squared. Therefore PV has the same unit as energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 10kg of copper by 1k is its
questions.explanation: Heat capacity is the heat required to raise the temperature of an entire body by 1 kelvin. Specific heat capacity is defined per unit mass, usually per kilogram. Since the question refers to 10 kg of copper as one whole sample, not to one kilogram, the correct property is the heat capacity of that body. Latent heat concerns change of state, not temperature rise.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A tap supplies water at 25oC while another supplies water at 75oC. If a man wishes to bathe with water at 40oC, the ratio of the mass of cold water to the mass of hot water required is
questions.explanation: Let the masses of cold and hot water be mc and mh. With no heat loss, heat gained by the cold water equals heat lost by the hot water. Thus mc times 40 minus 25 equals mh times 75 minus 40. So 15mc equals 35mh, giving mc divided by mh as 35 over 15, which simplifies to 7 over 3. The ratio cold to hot is therefore 7 to 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When heat is applied to one end of a metal rod, the molecules at the other end soon begin to vibrate with greater amplitude than before because heat has been transferred by
questions.explanation: In a metal rod, heating one end causes energy to pass through the material without bulk motion of the rod itself. Neighboring particles transfer vibrational energy, and in metals free electrons also help carry energy quickly. That mode of heat transfer is conduction. Convection requires fluid motion, radiation needs no medium, and evaporation is a surface process, so neither fits the situation described.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following media allow the transmission of sound wave through them i. Air. ii. Liquids. iii. Solids.
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it requires a material medium for transmission. Air supports sound because its particles can compress and rarefy. Liquids also transmit sound, and solids do as well, often more efficiently because their particles are closely packed. Since all three listed media can carry sound, the correct choice includes air, liquids, and solids together.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following properties is/are common to all waves? i. Diffraction ii. Refraction iii. Interference
questions.explanation: Diffraction, refraction, and interference are all standard wave behaviors. Diffraction is the spreading or bending of waves around edges and openings. Refraction occurs when wave speed changes as the wave enters another medium, causing a change in direction. Interference results from superposition when waves overlap. These phenomena apply to waves generally, whether mechanical or electromagnetic, so all three are common wave properties.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A piano wire 0.5m long has a total mass of 0.01kg and is stretched with a tension of 800N. Calculate the frequency of the wire when it sounds its fundamental note
questions.explanation: For the fundamental note of a stretched string, frequency equals one over twice the length multiplied by the square root of tension over linear density. The linear density is mass divided by length, so 0.01 divided by 0.5 equals 0.02 kilogram per metre. Then frequency is 1 over 1 multiplied by the square root of 800 over 0.02, which is the square root of 40000, giving 200 hertz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A note is called an octave of another note when
options: its frequency is twice that of the first note
its frequency is half of the first note
the notes have the same fundamental frequency
its periodic time is twice that of the first note
questions.explanation: In musical acoustics, a note one octave above another has double its frequency. If the original note has frequency f, its octave has frequency 2f. A note with half the frequency would be an octave below instead. Equal fundamental frequency would mean the same pitch, not an octave separation. Therefore the correct statement is that its frequency is twice that of the first note.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The speed of sound in air at sea level is 340ms\(^{-1}\) while that of light is 300 000kms\(^{-1}\). How far (to the nearest meter) from the center of a thunderstorm is an observer who hears a thunder 2s after a lightning flash?
questions.explanation: The delay arises because light from the lightning reaches the observer almost instantly compared with sound. So the storm distance is found from the sound travel only: distance equals speed times time. Using 340 metres per second and 2 seconds gives 680 metres. The listed speed of light merely justifies neglecting the light travel time over this short distance. Therefore the observer is about 680 metres away.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A slight loading of a tuning fork has the effect of
questions.explanation: Slight loading adds mass to the vibrating prongs of the tuning fork. Increasing the effective mass lowers the natural frequency of vibration, so the pitch falls. This is why adding a little wax to a tuning fork makes it produce a lower note. The main effect is on frequency rather than amplitude, so the correct result is a decrease in frequency.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two strings of the same length and under the same tension gives notes of frequencies in the ratio 4 : 1. The masses of the strings are in the corresponding ratio of
questions.explanation: For strings of the same length under the same tension, frequency is inversely proportional to the square root of mass per unit length. Since the lengths are equal, mass per unit length is proportional to total mass. Thus f is proportional to 1 over square root of m. If the frequencies are in the ratio 4 to 1, then the masses are in the inverse square ratio, 1 to 16.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object is placed 10cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15cm. What is the position and nature of the image formed?
questions.explanation: Using the Cartesian sign convention for mirrors, a concave mirror has focal length minus 15 centimetres and the object distance is minus 10 centimetres. From one over f equals one over u plus one over v, we get minus 1 over 15 equals minus 1 over 10 plus 1 over v. Hence 1 over v equals 1 over 30, so v equals plus 30 centimetres. Positive v means the image is behind the mirror and virtual.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following phenomena explains the formation of a mirage? i. Reflection ii. Refraction iii. Diffraction
questions.explanation: A mirage is caused by light traveling through layers of air at different temperatures and therefore different refractive indices. The ray bends continuously by refraction, and near the hottest layer it may undergo total internal reflection, giving the appearance of water. Diffraction is not involved. So the relevant phenomena are refraction and reflection only, making the first option the correct one.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When white light is dispersed by a spectrometer, the component having the shortest wavelength is
questions.explanation: In the visible spectrum, wavelength decreases from red toward violet. Therefore violet has the shortest wavelength among orange, green, violet, and red. Because frequency is inversely related to wavelength for light, violet also has the highest frequency of the listed colours. This agrees with standard dispersion of white light into its visible components. Hence violet is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statement is TRUE of ultraviolet, visible and infra-red rays?
options: they are all electromagnetic waves with the same wavelength
ultra-violet rays have shorter wavelengths than infra-red rays and produce flourescence
infrared rays have shorter wavelength than visible light and produce the sensation of heat
the wavelenghts increase in the sequence: visible, ultra-violet, infra-red
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet, visible, and infrared are all electromagnetic waves, but they do not share the same wavelength. Ultraviolet lies at shorter wavelengths than visible light, while infrared lies at longer wavelengths. Ultraviolet is well known for causing fluorescence in suitable materials. Therefore the statement that ultraviolet has shorter wavelengths than infrared and produces fluorescence is the true one. The other options contain wavelength-order errors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A spectrum of sunlight is said to be impure when
options: it is made of only three colours
it has no red colour in it
the different colours in it overlap
it does not contain white light
questions.explanation: A pure spectrum is one in which the colours are sharply separated, each wavelength region appearing distinctly. An impure spectrum occurs when adjacent colours overlap so that the separation is not clean. It is not defined by having only three colours, by lacking red, or by not containing white light. Therefore the correct description of an impure spectrum is that the different colours overlap.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A cell of internal resistance 2 ohms supplies current to a 6 ohms resistor. The efficiency of the cell is
questions.explanation: The efficiency of a cell delivering current to an external resistor is the ratio of useful power in the load to total power supplied by the cell. That simplifies to R divided by R plus r, where R is the external resistance and r the internal resistance. With R equal to 6 ohms and r equal to 2 ohms, efficiency is 6 over 8, which is 0.75 or 75 percent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a resistance R is across a cell, the voltage across the terminals of the cell is reduced to two-third of its normal value. The internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation: Let the cell emf be E and internal resistance r. With an external resistance R connected, the terminal voltage is ER divided by R plus r. The question says this terminal voltage is two thirds of the normal value, meaning two thirds of E. So R over R plus r equals 2 over 3. Solving gives 3R equals 2R plus 2r, hence r equals R over 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A household refrigerator is rated 200 watts. If electricity costs 5k per kWh, what is the cost of operating it in 20 days?
questions.explanation: A 200 watt refrigerator uses 0.2 kilowatt. In 20 days, the operating time is 20 times 24, which is 480 hours. Energy consumed is therefore 0.2 times 480 equals 96 kilowatt-hour. At 5 kobo per kilowatt-hour, the cost is 96 times 5 equals 480 kobo. Since 100 kobo make 1 naira, the total cost is 4.80 naira.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following ammeters may be used to measure alternating currents? i. moving-coil ammeter ii. moving-iron ammeter iii. hot-wire ammeter
questions.explanation: A moving-coil ammeter works properly only with direct current because reversing current reverses the torque, giving no steady deflection on alternating current. A moving-iron ammeter responds to the magnetic effect regardless of current direction, and a hot-wire ammeter responds to heating, which also does not depend on direction. Therefore the instruments suitable for measuring alternating current are the moving-iron and hot-wire ammeters only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The principle of operation of an induction coil is based on
questions.explanation: An induction coil works by electromagnetic induction. When the current in the primary changes, the magnetic flux linking the secondary changes, and an emf is induced in the secondary winding. This is exactly the content of Faraday’s law. Ohm’s law concerns voltage and resistance, Ampere’s law concerns magnetic fields due to currents, and Coulomb’s law concerns electric forces between charges. So Faraday’s law is the governing principle.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A dynamo primarily combines
questions.explanation: A dynamo is an electrical generator. It uses mechanical rotation to cut magnetic flux and thereby produce electrical energy by electromagnetic induction. So its essential energy conversion is from mechanical energy to electrical energy. Converting electrical energy to motion describes a motor, not a dynamo. The other options omit the electrical output entirely. Therefore the first option is the correct physical description.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a certain fusion reaction, a deuteron (\(^{2}_{1}H\)) interacts with a triton (\(^{3}_{1}He\)) and produces an a-particle (\(^{4}_{2}He\)) and a second product. The second product is
questions.explanation: Using the symbols exactly as printed, the reaction is deuterium 2 over 1 plus helium-3, 3 over 2, producing helium-4, 4 over 2, and another particle. Conserving mass number gives 2 plus 3 equals 4 plus A, so A equals 1. Conserving charge gives 1 plus 2 equals 2 plus Z, so Z equals 1. The missing particle is therefore hydrogen-1, a proton, not a neutron.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following symbolic representations is correct for an atom X with 22 electrons and 43 neutrons?
questions.explanation: For a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons, so the atomic number Z is 22. The number of neutrons is 43. Hence the mass number A is protons plus neutrons, 22 plus 43, giving 65. In standard nuclide notation, A is written as the superscript and Z as the subscript beside the symbol X. Therefore the correct representation is 65 over 22 X.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following units is equivalent to kgms-1?
questions.explanation: A newton is defined as kilogram metre per second squared. Multiplying this by second gives kilogram metre per second. Therefore newton second is equivalent to kilogram metre per second. By contrast, newton per second gives kilogram metre per second cubed, and joule per second is watt. So the only listed unit equivalent to kilogram metre per second is newton second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A jet engine develops a thrust of 270Ns when the velocity of the exhaust gases relative to the engine is 300ms-1. What is the mass of the material ejected per second?
questions.explanation: Thrust is the rate of change of momentum, so for exhaust gases moving at speed v relative to the engine, thrust F equals mass ejected per second times v. Rearranging gives mass per second as F divided by v. Using 270 newtons and 300 metres per second gives 270 over 300, which is 0.90 kilogram per second. Therefore the correct numerical option is 0.90 kilogram.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A man walks 8km north and then 5km in a direction 60o east of north. Find the distance from his starting point
questions.explanation: The second displacement is 5 kilometres at 60 degrees east of north. Its northward component is 5 cos 60, which is 2.5 kilometres, and its eastward component is 5 sin 60, about 4.33 kilometres. Total northward displacement is 8 plus 2.5, which is 10.5 kilometres. The resultant distance is the square root of 10.5 squared plus 4.33 squared, giving the square root of 129, about 11.36 kilometres.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An elevator of mass 4800kg is supported by a cable which can safely withstand a maximum tension of 60 000N. The maximum upward acceleration the elevator can have is
questions.explanation: For upward acceleration, the cable tension must overcome weight and provide the net force. So T minus mg equals ma. With mass 4800 kilograms and using g as 10 metres per second squared, the weight is 48000 newtons. The maximum safe tension is 60000 newtons, so the net upward force is 12000 newtons. Dividing by 4800 gives 2.5 metres per second squared as the maximum upward acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A constant force of 40N acting on a body initially at rest gives an acceleration of 0.1ms-2 for 4s. Calculate the work done by the force
questions.explanation: Work done by a constant force in the direction of motion equals force times displacement. Starting from rest, the displacement in 4 seconds under acceleration 0.1 metre per second squared is s equals one half times a times t squared, which is 0.5 times 0.1 times 16 equals 0.8 metre. Multiplying by the 40 newton force gives 32 joules. That matches the third option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body rolls down a slope from a height of 100m. its velocity at the foot of the slope is 20ms-1. What percentage of its initial potential energy is converted into kinetic energy? [g = 10ms-1]
questions.explanation: The initial potential energy is mgh, which here is m times 10 times 100, equal to 1000m joules. At the bottom, the kinetic energy is one half mv squared, or one half times m times 20 squared, equal to 200m joules. The fraction converted is 200m divided by 1000m, which is 0.2. Expressed as a percentage, that is 20 percent. The mass cancels out throughout.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The coefficient of static friction between a 40kg crate and concrete surface is 0.25. Find the magnitude of the minimum force needed to keep the crate stationary on the concrete base inclined at 45o to the horizontal. [G = 10ms-1]
questions.explanation: The crate tends to slide down the 45 degree incline. Its downslope weight component is mg sin 45, which is 40 times 10 times 0.707, about 283 newtons. The normal reaction is mg cos 45, also about 283 newtons, so the maximum static friction is 0.25 times 283, about 70.7 newtons acting up the slope. The minimum extra upward force needed is 283 minus 70.7, about 212 newtons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a beaker is filled with water it is observed that the surface of the water is not horizontal at the glass-water interface. This behavior is due to
questions.explanation: The water surface curves near the glass because molecules at the surface experience surface tension, while adhesion between water and glass makes the liquid climb slightly at the walls. This produces a meniscus instead of a perfectly flat surface all the way to the edge. Friction and viscosity relate to motion within fluids, and evaporation concerns escape of molecules, so they do not explain the observed shape.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The mechanical advantage(MA) of an inclined plane depends on
options: the product of its length and height
the ratio of its length to its height
questions.explanation: For an ideal inclined plane, the effort times the length of the plane equals the load times the vertical height. Rearranging gives mechanical advantage, load divided by effort, equal to length divided by height. So the mechanical advantage depends on the ratio of its length to its height, not on either quantity separately and not on their product. Therefore the fourth option is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A load of 5N gives an extension of 0.56cm in a wire which obeys Hooke's law. What is the extension caused by a load of 20N?
questions.explanation: A wire obeying Hooke’s law has extension directly proportional to load, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded. Increasing the load from 5 newtons to 20 newtons multiplies the load by 4. Therefore the extension must also be multiplied by 4. So the new extension is 4 times 0.56 centimetre, which equals 2.24 centimetres. This corresponds to the third option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A cube of side 10cm and mass 0.5kg floats in a liquid with only \(\frac{1}{5}\) of its height above the liquid surface. What is the relative density of the liquid?
questions.explanation: If one fifth of the cube is above the liquid, then four fifths is submerged. For a floating body, the fraction submerged equals the density of the body divided by the density of the liquid. The cube’s volume is 10 centimetres cubed, meaning 1000 cubic centimetres, and its mass is 0.5 kilogram or 500 grams, so its density is 0.5 gram per cubic centimetre. Dividing by four fifths gives liquid relative density 0.625.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The distance between the fixed points of a centigrade thermometer is 20cm. What is the temperature when the mercury level is 4.5cm above the lower mark?
questions.explanation: On the centigrade scale, the lower and upper fixed points represent 0 degrees Celsius and 100 degrees Celsius. If these marks are 20 centimetres apart, then each centimetre corresponds to 100 divided by 20, which is 5 degrees Celsius. A mercury level 4.5 centimetres above the lower mark therefore indicates 4.5 times 5, giving 22.5 degrees Celsius. So the first option is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The length of a side of a metallic cube at 20ºC is 5.0cm. Given that the linear expansivity of the metal is 4.0 x 10\(^{-5}\)k\(^{-1}\), find the volume of the cube at 120°C.
questions.explanation: The cube initially has volume 5.0 cubed, which is 125 cubic centimetres. The temperature rise is 120 minus 20, so 100 kelvin. For an isotropic solid, the cubical expansivity is approximately three times the linear expansivity, giving 3 times 4.0 times 10 to the minus 5, or 1.2 times 10 to the minus 4 per kelvin. Hence the new volume is 125 times 1.012, equal to 126.50 cubic centimetres.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: As a result of air at the top of a barometer, the height of the mercury column is 73.5cm when it should be 75.0cm; the volume of the space above the mercury is 8.0cm3. Calculate the correct barometer height when the barometer reads 74.0cm and the volume of the space above the mercury is 6.0cm3.
questions.explanation: The trapped air above the mercury lowers the observed barometer height by exerting pressure. In the first state, the correct height should be 75.0 centimetres but the reading is 73.5 centimetres, so the trapped air pressure is 1.5 centimetres of mercury when its volume is 8.0 cubic centimetres. By Boyle’s law, PV is constant, so 1.5 times 8.0 equals 2.0 times 6.0. Thus at the second state the air pressure is 2.0 centimetres, making the correct height 74.0 plus 2.0 equals 76.0 centimetres.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Hot water is added to three times its mass of water at 10oC and the resultant temperature is 20oC. What is the initial temperature of the hot water?
questions.explanation: Let the mass of hot water be m and the colder water be 3m at 10 degrees Celsius. With no heat loss and equal specific heat capacities, heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cold water: m(T - 20) = 3m(20 - 10). Hence T - 20 = 30, so T = 50 degrees Celsius. Therefore the correct option is index 2.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: 22,000J of heat is required to raise the temperature of 1.5kg of paraffin from 20oC to 30oC. Calculate the specific heat capacity of paraffin.
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is found from c equals Q divided by m times temperature rise. Here Q is 22000 joules, m is 1.5 kilograms, and the temperature increase is 30 minus 20, which is 10 degrees Celsius. So c equals 22000 divided by 15, giving 1466.7 joules per kilogram per degree Celsius. This rounds to about 1466, matching the first option closely.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In which of the following are the substance arranged in descending order of their thermal conductivities?
questions.explanation: Among the listed substances, copper is the best thermal conductor, steel conducts heat less well than copper but much better than glass, and glass is a poor conductor. Therefore in descending order of thermal conductivity, the correct sequence is copper, steel, glass. Any arrangement placing glass ahead of either metal or steel ahead of copper contradicts known material properties. Hence the first option is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The vacuum in a thermos flask helps to reduce heat transfer by?
questions.explanation: A vacuum contains essentially no particles, so it suppresses both conduction and convection, since both require matter. Heat radiation, however, can pass through empty space, which is why thermos flasks also use reflective surfaces to reduce it. The question asks specifically what the vacuum reduces, and that is conduction and convection. Therefore the correct option is the one pairing those two modes.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following phenomena explains the fact that a house whose roof is coated with white paint will be cooler in the hot season than one coated with black paint ?
questions.explanation: White paint reflects a large fraction of incoming solar radiation, whereas black paint absorbs much more of it. Because the white-coated roof absorbs less radiant energy, less heat is transferred into the house and the interior stays cooler during hot weather. This is explained chiefly by reflection, not conduction, convection, or refraction. Therefore the correct phenomenon is reflection.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wave has a frequency of 2Hz and a wavelength of 30cm. The velocity of the wave is
questions.explanation: Wave speed is given by v equals f times wavelength. The frequency is 2 hertz and the wavelength is 30 centimetres, which must be converted to 0.30 metre before substitution. Multiplying gives 2 times 0.30 equals 0.60 metre per second. The unit conversion is essential; using centimetres directly would produce the wrong SI answer. Therefore the correct option is 0.6 metre per second.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A boat at anchor is rocked by waves whose crest are 100m apart and whose velocity is 25ms-1. At what interval does the wave crest reach the boat?
questions.explanation: The distance between successive crests is the wavelength, 100 metres. The time interval between crests arriving at the anchored boat is the period, found from period equals wavelength divided by speed. Using 100 metres and 25 metres per second gives 100 divided by 25, which is 4 seconds. So the crests reach the boat every 4.00 seconds. That corresponds to the third option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following instruments has a pure tone?
questions.explanation: A pure tone contains essentially one frequency. A tuning fork is the standard source of a nearly pure tone because it vibrates predominantly at a single frequency with relatively few overtones. A guitar or other vibrating strings usually produce a fundamental together with harmonics, and a siren also generates a more complex sound. Therefore the instrument associated with a pure tone is the tuning fork.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The lowest note emitted by a stretched string has a frequency of 40Hz. How many overtones are there between 40Hz and 150Hz?
questions.explanation: The lowest note is the fundamental, 40 hertz. Harmonics occur at whole-number multiples of this frequency: 80 hertz, 120 hertz, 160 hertz, and so on. Overtones are the harmonics above the fundamental. Between 40 hertz and 150 hertz, the allowed overtones are 80 hertz and 120 hertz only. The next one, 160 hertz, is above 150 hertz. Therefore there are two overtones in that range.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements supports the assumption that light travels in straight lines?
options: a source of light produces distinct shadows of opaque objects
a source of light produces interference patterns on a suitably placed screen
questions.explanation: Distinct shadows support rectilinear propagation because an opaque object blocks light traveling along straight paths, leaving a well-defined region where rays do not reach. Diffraction and interference instead demonstrate wave behavior, and reflection only shows what happens at a surface after incidence. A sharp shadow is therefore the direct observational evidence that light ordinarily travels in straight lines.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If an object is placed in front of two mirrors inclined at 90o, how many images will be formed?
questions.explanation: For two plane mirrors inclined at angle theta, when 360 divided by theta is an integer, the number of images is 360 over theta minus 1. Here theta is 90 degrees, so the number of images is 360 over 90 minus 1, which equals 4 minus 1 = 3. Therefore the object forms three images between the two mirrors.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object 3.0cm high is placed 60.0cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0cm. Calculate the size of the image formed
questions.explanation: Apply the thin lens equation for a converging lens with a real object: 1 over f = 1 over u + 1 over v. With f = 20 cm and u = 60 cm, 1 over v = 1 over 20 minus 1 over 60 = 1 over 30, so v = 30 cm. Magnification magnitude is v over u = 30 over 60 = 0.5. Image size = 0.5 × 3.0 cm = 1.5 cm, inverted.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A pool of water appears to be 1.0m deep when viewed vertically from above. If the refractive index of water is 1.33, what is the actual depth of the pool?
questions.explanation: When viewed normally from air into water, refractive index equals real depth divided by apparent depth. The pool appears 1.0 m deep and water has refractive index 1.33, so real depth = 1.33 times 1.0 m = 1.33 m. The pool looks shallower because refraction bends light away from the normal as it leaves the water. Hence the actual depth is 1.330 m.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A ray of light is incident at an angle of 30o on one top surface of a parallel-sided glass block of refractive index 1.5. The ray finally emerges from the lower surface. What is the angular deviation of the emergent ray?
questions.explanation: A ray passing through a parallel-sided glass block emerges parallel to its original direction because the two refracting faces are parallel. The ray may suffer lateral displacement, but its final direction is unchanged. Angular deviation means the angle between the original incident direction and the emergent direction. Since those directions are parallel, the angular deviation is zero degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Four lenses are being considered for use as a microscope objective. Which of the following focal lengths is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A microscope objective must be a converging lens so that it can form a magnified real intermediate image of a nearby object. Therefore the focal length must be positive, not negative. Greater magnification requires a short focal length, so +5 mm is more suitable than +5 cm. The best choice is the short focal length converging lens, +5 mm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the angle of declination in a place is 10oE, calculate the true geographic bearing if the compass reads N40oE
questions.explanation: An easterly declination of 10 degrees means magnetic north is 10 degrees east of true north. The compass reading N40E is measured from magnetic north, so the line is 40 degrees east of magnetic north. Relative to true north, the direction is therefore 10 degrees plus 40 degrees east, giving N50E. The supplied key is correct and the draft subtraction was the sign error.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two capacitance of 6\(\mu\)F and 8\(\mu\)F are connected in series. What additional capacitance must be connected in series with this combination to give a total of 3\(\mu\)F
questions.explanation: First combine the 6 microfarad and 8 microfarad capacitors in series: 1 over C = 1 over 6 + 1 over 8 = 7 over 24, so C = 24 over 7 microfarad. Let the added series capacitor be x. Then 1 over 3 = 1 over (24 over 7) + 1 over x = 7 over 24 + 1 over x. Hence 1 over x = 1 over 24 and x = 24 microfarad.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a transformer has more secondary windings than primary windings, it?
questions.explanation: If the secondary has more turns than the primary, the transformer is step-up, so the secondary voltage is greater than the primary voltage. For an ideal transformer, power input is approximately equal to power output, so a higher secondary voltage must be accompanied by a lower secondary current. Therefore the true statement is that it has a smaller secondary current.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A current of 0.5A flows through a resistor when connected to a 40-V battery. How much energy is dissipated in 2 minutes?
questions.explanation: Electrical energy dissipated is E = VIt. Here V = 40 V, I = 0.5 A, and time is 2 minutes = 120 s. So E = 40 times 0.5 times 120 = 20 times 120 = 2400 J. The units are correct because volt times ampere gives watt, and watt times second gives joule. Thus the resistor dissipates 2400 J.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The direction of the magnetic field at a point in the vicinity of a bar magnet is
options: always towards the north pole of the magnet
always away from the south pole of the magnet
along the line joining the point to the neutral point
in the direction the north pole of a compass needle would point
questions.explanation: Magnetic field direction at a point is defined operationally as the direction in which the north-seeking pole of a small compass would point when placed there. That definition works for any magnetic field geometry. It is not always simply toward the north pole of a magnet or away from the south pole. Therefore the correct statement is the compass-needle direction.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When two parallel wires carry currents in opposite directions, the force on either wire is
options: zero, because the currents cancel each other
twice as much as when the currents are in the same direction
questions.explanation: Parallel current-carrying wires attract when currents flow in the same direction and repel when currents flow in opposite directions. Since the currents here are opposite, each wire experiences a force pushing it away from the other. The force is not zero because the magnetic fields still interact. Therefore the correct answer is that the force on either wire is away from the other wire.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A galvanometer of resistance 20\(\Omega\) is to be provided with a shunt that \(\frac{1}{10}\) of the whole current in a circuit passes through the galvanometer. The resistance of the shunt is
questions.explanation: The shunt is connected in parallel with the galvanometer, so both have the same potential difference. If one tenth of the total current passes through the galvanometer, then nine tenths passes through the shunt, so Is over Ig = 9. Using IgRg = IsRs gives Rs = Ig over Is times Rg = 1 over 9 times 20 ohm = 20 over 9 ohm = 2.22 ohm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is TRUE of photoelectric effect?
options: the energy of the emitted electrons is independent of the work function of the surface
the energy of the emitted electron depends on the wavelength of the incident light
the greater the intensity of the incuident light, the greater the incident of the emitted electron
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is given by hf minus the work function. Since frequency f equals c over wavelength, the emitted electron energy depends on the wavelength of the incident light. It is not independent of the work function, and increasing intensity mainly increases the number of emitted electrons, not their maximum energy. Therefore option 2 is true.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Isotopes are nuclei which have
options: the same number of nuetrons and electrons
equal number of electrons and protons
the same atomic number but different number of neutrons
the same number of total particles
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so they must have the same number of protons, which means the same atomic number. They differ in the number of neutrons, which changes the mass number. Equal electrons and protons only describes a neutral atom in general and is not the defining feature of isotopes. Hence the correct statement is same atomic number but different neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A radioactive sample initially contains N atoms. After three half-lives the number of atoms that have disintegrated is
questions.explanation: After n half-lives, the remaining number of atoms is N times one half to the power n. For three half-lives, remaining atoms = N times 1 over 2 cubed = N over 8. The number disintegrated is the initial amount minus the remaining amount: N minus N over 8 = 7N over 8. Therefore the correct answer is 7N over 8.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct precision if the length of a piece of wire is measured with a meter rule?
questions.explanation: A meter rule is normally graduated in millimetres, so its least count is 1 mm. A length measured directly with it should therefore be recorded to the nearest millimetre. Writing 35 mm is consistent with that instrument precision. The alternatives 35.0 mm, 35.00 mm, and 35.01 mm imply precisions of 0.1 mm, 0.01 mm, and 0.01 mm respectively, which a meter rule cannot justify.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A heavy object is suspended from a string and lowered into water so that it is completely submerged. The object appears lighter because
options: the density of water is less than that of the object
the pressure is low just below the water surface
the tension in the string neutralizes part of the weight
questions.explanation: A fully submerged object experiences an upward buoyant force due to the fluid pressure being greater at lower depths than at higher depths. This upthrust reduces the apparent weight, so the object seems lighter when immersed. The effect is explained by Archimedes' principle, not simply by low pressure near the surface or by the string neutralizing the weight. Therefore the object appears lighter because it experiences an upthrust.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is a derived unit?
questions.explanation: A derived unit is built from base SI units through a physical relation. Newton is the unit of force, and from force equals mass times acceleration, 1 newton equals 1 kilogram metre per second squared. Kilogram, metre, and kelvin are base units, not derived units. Therefore the derived unit among the options is newton.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two objects, one having three times the mass of the other, are dropped at the same time from a tall building. When they are above the ground, the two objects will have the same?
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, all objects near the Earth fall with the same acceleration g regardless of mass. Momentum equals mv, kinetic energy equals one half mv squared, and potential energy equals mgh, so those quantities depend on mass and will differ for objects whose masses are in a 3 to 1 ratio. The only quantity guaranteed to be the same is acceleration.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is in a neutral equilibrium?
options: a heavy weight suspended on a string
a cone resting on its slant edge
the beam of a balance in use
questions.explanation: Neutral equilibrium means that after a small displacement the body stays in its new position because the height of its center of gravity does not change. A cone resting on its slant edge satisfies this condition. A heavy weight suspended on a string and a heavy-based table lamp are stable, while a balance beam in use is made very sensitive rather than neutral. Thus the cone is the neutral case.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically into the air with an initial velocity u. What is the greatest height reached?
questions.explanation: At the greatest height, the vertical velocity becomes zero. Using the kinematic relation v squared = u squared minus 2gh for upward motion under gravity, set v = 0 to obtain 0 = u squared minus 2gh. Rearranging gives h = u squared over 2g. The sign is consistent because gravity opposes the initial upward motion. Hence the maximum height is u squared over 2g.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following assumptions is made in a simple pendulum experiment? the
options: initial angle of oscillation must be large
questions.explanation: A simple pendulum is idealized by assuming a small angular displacement, a bob treated as a point mass, negligible air resistance, and a light inextensible string. Therefore the statement that the suspending string is inextensible is a valid assumption. The bob is not assumed to have finite size, and a large initial angle would invalidate the simple small-angle treatment.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A constant force of magnitude F acts on an object of mass 0.04kg initially at rest at a point O. if the speed of the object when it has moved 50m from O is 500ms-1, what is the value of F?
questions.explanation: The object starts from rest and reaches 500 m per second after moving 50 m under a constant force. From v squared = u squared + 2as, 500 squared = 2 times a times 50, so a = 2500 m per second squared. Then F = ma = 0.04 times 2500 = 100 N. The force therefore has magnitude 100.0 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A rectangular tank contains water to a depth of 2m, if the base is 4m x 3m, calculate the force on the base (Density of water = 103kgm-3, g = 10ms-2)
questions.explanation: Pressure at the base of the water is p = rho gh = 10 to the 3 times 10 times 2 = 2.0 times 10 to the 4 pascal. The base area is 4 times 3 = 12 square metres. Hence force on the base is F = pA = 2.0 times 10 to the 4 times 12 = 2.4 times 10 to the 5 N, which is also written as 24 times 10 to the 4 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 1000kg elevator is descending vertically with an acceleration of 1.0ms-2, if the acceleration due to gravity is 10ms-2, the tension in the suspending cable is
questions.explanation: For a descending elevator accelerating downward at 1.0 m per second squared, weight acts downward and tension upward. Taking downward as positive, mg minus T = ma. With m = 1000 kg and g = 10 m per second squared, 10000 minus T = 1000. Therefore T = 9000 N. The tension is less than the weight because the elevator accelerates downward.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The mode of heat transfer which does not require a material medium is
questions.explanation: Radiation transfers heat by electromagnetic waves and therefore does not require a material medium. That is why thermal energy from the Sun can reach the Earth through space. Conduction and convection both require matter to carry energy. Propagation is not one of the standard heat-transfer modes here. Therefore the only correct choice is radiation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The expansion of solids can be considered a disadvantage in the?
questions.explanation: Thermal expansion is undesirable in a balance wheel of a watch because changes in size alter the timing properties and reduce accuracy. In the fitting of wheels on rims, fire alarms, and thermostats, expansion is intentionally used to produce a useful effect. The question asks for a disadvantage, so the correct choice is the balance wheel of a watch.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is the amount of heat required to
options: melt lead at its melting point
heat a unit mass of lead through 1oC
change the state of a unit mass of lead at its melting point
change the state of a unit mass of lead at its boiling point
questions.explanation: Specific latent heat of fusion is the heat required per unit mass to change a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point without any temperature change. Therefore the essential features are unit mass, change of state, and melting point. It is not the heat to raise temperature by 1 degree, and it does not refer to boiling point. Hence option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is common to evaporation and boiling? They
options: take place at a definite pressure
questions.explanation: Evaporation and boiling both convert a liquid into vapour, so both involve a change of state. However, evaporation can occur at any temperature and is mainly a surface phenomenon, whereas boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a definite temperature for a given pressure. Since those features differ, their common property is simply that both involve change of state.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Mercury is suitable as a barometric fluid because it?
options: is several times denser than water
is a good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: A barometer works by balancing atmospheric pressure with the pressure of a liquid column, so p = rho gh. A very dense liquid gives the same pressure with a much shorter and more practical column. Mercury is suitable because it is far denser than water. Its opacity and thermal conductivity are not the main reason for its use as a barometric fluid.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following properties makes metals ideal for cooking utensils?
questions.explanation: Cooking utensils should transfer heat efficiently from the flame or hot plate to the food. Metals are ideal mainly because they are good conductors of heat, so heating is rapid and fairly uniform. A high coefficient of expansion is not desirable, low specific heat capacity is not the essential general reason, and poor radiation of heat is irrelevant here. Therefore option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A gas occupies a volume of 300cm3at a temperature of 27oC. What is its volume at 54oC, when the pressure is constant?
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, Charles' law applies: V over T is constant when temperature is measured in kelvin. Convert 27 degrees Celsius to 300 K and 54 degrees Celsius to 327 K. Then V2 = 300 cubic centimetres times 327 over 300 = 327 cubic centimetres. Using Celsius directly would be incorrect. Therefore the gas volume at 54 degrees Celsius is 327 cubic centimetres.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When two objects P and Q are supplied with the same quantity of heat, the temperature change in P is observed to be twice that of Q. The mass of P is half that of Q. The ratio of the specific heat capacity of P to Q is
questions.explanation: For each object, the heat supplied is Q = mc delta T. Since the same quantity of heat is supplied, mP cP delta TP = mQ cQ delta TQ. Given delta TP is twice delta TQ and mP is half mQ, substitution gives one half mQ times cP times 2 delta TQ = mQ cQ delta TQ. This simplifies to cP = cQ, so the ratio is 1 to 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A lens of focal length 12.0cm forms an upright image three times the size of a real object. The distance between the object and the images is
questions.explanation: An upright image formed by a lens is virtual, so the lens must be converging with the object inside the focal length. The linear magnification is 3, so the image distance magnitude is three times the object distance. Using 1 over f = 1 over u minus 1 over v with f = 12 cm and v = 3u gives u = 8 cm and v = 24 cm. Their separation is 24 minus 8 = 16 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In which of the following arrangements is the wavelength in an increasing order?
options: Gamma rays, infra-red rays, x-rays, radiowaves
Gamma rays, x-rays, infra-red ray, radiowaves
Radiowaves, x-rays, gamma ray, infra-red rays
Infra-red rays, radiowaves, x-rays, gamma rays
questions.explanation: The electromagnetic spectrum arranged in increasing wavelength begins with gamma rays, followed by x-rays, then longer-wavelength regions such as infra-red, and finally radiowaves among the types listed. Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and radiowaves the longest. Therefore the only arrangement in correct increasing order is gamma rays, x-rays, infra-red rays, radiowaves.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the refractive index of glass is 1.5, what is the critical angle at the air-glass interface?
questions.explanation: The critical angle applies for light traveling from the denser medium to the rarer one, here from glass to air. It satisfies sine c = n2 over n1 = 1.0 over 1.5 = 2 over 3. Therefore c = sine inverse of 2 over 3. The ratio is correctly less than 1, so the result is physically admissible. Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the effect of the increase in the size of the hole of a pin-hole camera on the image? it
options: brings the image into a sharper focus
questions.explanation: A pin-hole camera produces a sharp image only when the aperture is very small. If the hole becomes larger, light from one object point spreads over a larger patch on the screen and overlaps with light from neighboring points. This overlap reduces definition and causes blurring. Increasing the hole size therefore does not sharpen or magnify the image; it gives a blurred image.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A pencil is placed vertically between a concave mirror and its focal point. The image of the pencil in the mirror will be
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, if the object is placed between the pole and the focal point, the reflected rays diverge and their backward extensions meet behind the mirror. The image formed is therefore virtual and erect. Because the image is larger than the object in this arrangement, it is enlarged. Hence the correct description is virtual, erect and enlarged.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wave of frequency 10Hz forms a stationary wave pattern in a medium where the velocity is 20cms-1. The distance between adjacent nodes is
questions.explanation: Wave speed is given by v = f lambda. With v = 20 cm per second and f = 10 Hz, lambda = 20 over 10 = 2 cm. In a stationary wave, adjacent nodes are separated by half a wavelength. Therefore node spacing = 2 over 2 = 1 cm. So the distance between adjacent nodes is 1.0 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is true of the loudness of sound? It
options: depends on the square of the amplitude of the vibrating body
is proportional to the distance of the observer from the source of the sound
questions.explanation: Loudness is related to the intensity of sound, and for a vibrating source the intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude. Therefore a larger amplitude generally produces a louder sound. Loudness does not increase with distance from the source, and sound cannot travel in vacuum, so the vacuum-based options are false. Thus the true statement is that loudness depends on the square of amplitude.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A man clapping his hands at regular intervals observes that the echo of a clap coincides with the next clap. If the reflecting cliff is 160m away and the speed of sound is 320ms-1, what is the frequency of the clapping?
questions.explanation: An echo takes the sound to the cliff and back, so the clap travels 2 × 160 = 320 m before returning. With speed of sound 320 m/s, the echo time is 320/320 = 1 s. Because that echo coincides with the next clap, the clapping period is 1 s. Frequency is the reciprocal of period, so f = 1/1 = 1 Hz. Option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The vibration of an air column produces the sound in the
questions.explanation: A flute is a wind instrument in which sound is produced by the vibration of a column of air inside the tube. In contrast, a piano and a guitar mainly produce sound from vibrating strings, while a handbell produces sound from a vibrating metal body. Therefore the instrument whose sound comes from an air column is the flute.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of a d.c. electric motor?
questions.explanation: A direct-current electric motor contains a field magnet, an armature or coil, and a split-ring commutator with brushes. These parts are necessary to produce torque and maintain rotation in one direction. A transformer is a separate device used mainly with alternating current to change voltage levels. It is not a component part of a d.c. motor. Therefore transformer is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is stored by a dry Leclanche cell?
questions.explanation: A dry Leclanche cell stores energy in chemical form. During operation, chemical reactions inside the cell convert that stored chemical energy into electrical energy supplied to the external circuit. A cell does not store electric current, electrical power, or kinetic energy. Therefore the quantity stored by the dry cell is chemical energy.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is true of magnetism?
options: Iron fillings cling mainly round the ends of a bar magnet
The freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest in the geographic north-south direction
questions.explanation: Iron filings accumulate most strongly near the ends of a bar magnet because the magnetic field is strongest at the poles. A freely suspended magnet aligns approximately with magnetic north-south, not exactly geographic north-south. Like poles repel rather than attract, and lodestone is naturally magnetic iron oxide, not non-magnetic. Therefore the true statement is that iron filings cling mainly round the ends of a bar magnet.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The angle between the magnetic meridian and the geographic meridian at a locality on the earth is the
options: angle of inclination at the locality
angle of declination of the locality
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is defined as the horizontal angle between the geographic meridian, based on true north, and the magnetic meridian, based on magnetic north, at a place. Longitude and latitude merely specify position on Earth, while inclination refers to dip relative to the horizontal. Therefore the required angle is the angle of declination of the locality.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The sign of the change on a charged glass rod may be determined with
questions.explanation: To determine the sign of charge on an object, the testing instrument must already carry a known charge. With a charged electroscope, bringing the charged glass rod near the cap increases leaf divergence for like charge and reduces it for unlike charge. An uncharged electroscope can show that a body is charged but cannot reliably identify the sign. Hence a charged electroscope is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the inclination at Ibadan is 7oS, this means that
options: the angle between the geographic meridian and the magnetic meridian at Ibadan is 7o
the earth's magnetic intensity at Ibadan makes angle 7o with the horizontal direction
a magnetic needle will be inclined at 7o to the vertical at Ibadan
the north pole of a magnetic needle dips downward at Ibadan
questions.explanation: Magnetic inclination or dip is the angle made by Earth’s magnetic field with the horizontal plane at a locality. Thus an inclination of 7 degrees south means the field direction is inclined by 7 degrees to the horizontal there. It is not the angle between geographic and magnetic meridians, which would be declination, and it is not an angle to the vertical.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The wavelength of ultraviolet radiation is 400nm. If the speed of light in air is 3 x 10\(^8\)ms\(^{-1}\), then the frequency of the ultraviolet radiation is
questions.explanation: Use the wave relation speed equals frequency times wavelength. The wavelength is 400 nm, which is 400 x 10^-9 m or 4 x 10^-7 m. Hence frequency equals 3 x 10^8 divided by 4 x 10^-7, giving 0.75 x 10^15 Hz, that is 7.5 x 10^14 Hz. The units and power of ten are consistent with ultraviolet radiation.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is most strongly deflected by magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Magnetic deflection depends on charge and inversely on mass for moving particles. Gamma rays and X rays are uncharged electromagnetic radiation, so they are not deflected by a magnetic field. Beta particles are electrons or positrons and have charge with very small mass, so they undergo the strongest deflection among the listed options. Therefore beta particles are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental S.I unit?
questions.explanation: The SI base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, and candela. Meter, ampere, kelvin, and second are therefore fundamental units. Radian is an SI derived unit for plane angle, treated as dimensionless, not one of the base units. So the option that is not a fundamental SI unit is radian.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A simple pendulum with a period of 2.0s has its length doubled. Its new period is
questions.explanation: For a simple pendulum, the period is proportional to the square root of its length. Doubling the length multiplies the period by square root of 2. Starting from 2.0 s, the new period is 2.0 x 1.414, which is about 2.83 s. The result is larger, not doubled, because the dependence is on square root of length, not length itself.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following types of motion are oscillatory? i.a diving board when used by a diver. ii. the motion of the balance wheel of a wrist watch. iii. the motion of the turn-table of a record player. iv. the motion of the center of a ten kobo piece as it rolls down an inclined plane. v. the motion of the needle of a D.C. ammeter into which a low A.C. current is passed
questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion is repeated to and fro motion about an equilibrium position. A diving board vibrates after use, so it oscillates. A wristwatch balance wheel oscillates angularly. A turntable rotates continuously, not to and fro. The centre of a rolling coin translates down the plane, so it is not oscillatory. An ammeter needle on low AC swings alternately, so it oscillates. Hence i, ii and v are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 10ms-2 for ten seconds, the distance it covers in the last one second of its motion is
questions.explanation: For motion from rest with uniform acceleration, distance after time t is one half a t squared. In 10 s, the car travels 0.5 x 10 x 10^2 = 500 m. In 9 s, it travels 0.5 x 10 x 9^2 = 405 m. The distance covered in the last second is 500 minus 405, giving 95 m. The units are consistent.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A metal block of mass 5kg lies on a rough horizontal platform. If a horizontal force of 8N applied to the block through its center of mass just slides the block on the platform, then the coefficient of limiting friction between the block and platform is
questions.explanation: At the point of just sliding, the applied force equals the limiting friction. On a horizontal plane, limiting friction is mu times the normal reaction, and the reaction equals mg. Using m = 5 kg and the standard school value g = 10 m s^-2 gives R = 50 N. Hence mu = 8 divided by 50, which is 0.16. The coefficient is dimensionless.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a force?
questions.explanation: Friction, tension, upthrust, and weight are all forces and are measured in newtons. Impulse is not a force; it is the product of force and time and equals the change in momentum. Its unit is newton second, not newton. Therefore the quantity listed that is not a force is impulse.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two masses 40g and 60g respectively, are attached firmly to the ends of the light meter rule. The center of gravity of the system is
options: at the mid-point of the meter rule
indeterninate because the meter-rule is light
questions.explanation: Treat the meter rule as light, so only the two end masses matter. Place 40 g at 0 cm and 60 g at 100 cm. The centre of mass is at x = (40 x 0 + 60 x 100) divided by 100, which is 60 cm from the lighter mass. Since the ends are 100 cm apart, this is 40 cm from the heavier mass. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 0.05kg bullet travelling at 500ms-1 horizontally strikes a thick vertical wall. It stops after penetrating through the wall horizontal distance of 0.25m. What is the magnitude of the average force the wall exerts on the bullet?
questions.explanation: The wall brings the bullet to rest, so the work done by the average resisting force equals the loss of kinetic energy. Thus F times 0.25 equals one half times 0.05 times 500 squared. The kinetic energy is 6250 J, and dividing by 0.25 m gives 25000 N. The magnitude of the average force exerted by the wall is therefore 25000 N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A force of 100N stretches an elastic string to a total length of 20cm. If an additional force of 100N stretches the string 5cm further, Find the natural length of the string
questions.explanation: Let the natural length be L. Under 100 N, the total length becomes 20 cm, so the extension is 20 minus L. Under 200 N, the total length is 25 cm because the extra 100 N adds 5 cm, so the extension is 25 minus L. By Hooke’s law, doubling the force doubles the extension: 25 minus L equals 2 times 20 minus L. Solving gives L = 15 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two divers G and H are at depths 20m and 40m respectively below the water surface in a lake. The pressure on G is P1 while the pressure on H is P2. If the atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 10m of water, then the value of \( \frac{p_2}{p_1} \) is?
questions.explanation: Pressure at a depth in water equals atmospheric pressure plus hydrostatic pressure. Since atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 10 m of water, the total pressure on G at 20 m corresponds to 30 m of water, while on H at 40 m it corresponds to 50 m of water. Therefore p2 over p1 equals 50 divided by 30, which is 5 over 3 or about 1.67.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The areas of the effort and load pistons of a hydraulic press are 0.5m2 and 5m2 respectively. If a force F1 of 100N is applied on the effort piston, the force F2 on the load is
questions.explanation: A hydraulic press works by equal transmission of pressure. Therefore F1 divided by A1 equals F2 divided by A2. With F1 = 100 N, A1 = 0.5 m^2 and A2 = 5 m^2, the area ratio is 10. Hence F2 = 100 x 10 = 1000 N. The result is larger on the load side because the load piston has the greater area.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A uniform cylindrical block of wood floats in water with one-third of its height above the water level, in a liquid of relative density 0.8, what fraction of its height will be above the liquid level?
questions.explanation: If one third of the wood is above water, then two thirds is submerged in water. Hence the relative density of the wood is two thirds. In a liquid of relative density 0.8, the submerged fraction is wood density divided by liquid density, so two thirds divided by 0.8 equals five sixths. Therefore the fraction above the liquid is 1 minus five sixths, which is one sixth.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A thin aluminum plate has a surface area of 1.500m at 20ºC. What will be its surface area when it is cooled to -20ºC? (Take the linear expansivity of aluminum to be 2.5 x 10-5k-1).
questions.explanation: For a thin plate, area expansivity is about twice the linear expansivity. Thus beta = 2 x 2.5 x 10^-5 = 5.0 x 10^-5 K^-1. The temperature change is minus 40 K from 20 degrees C to minus 20 degrees C. So the new area is 1.500 x [1 + beta delta T] = 1.500 x 0.998 = 1.497 m^2. Cooling reduces the area slightly.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two liquids, P at a temperature of 20oC and Q at a temperature of 80oC have specific heat capacities of 1.0Jkg-1oC-1 and 1.5J kg-1 oC-1respectively. if equal masses of P and Q are mixed in a lagged calorimeter, then the equilibrium temperature is
questions.explanation: In a lagged calorimeter, heat lost by the hotter liquid equals heat gained by the cooler liquid. For equal masses, 1.5 times 80 minus theta equals 1.0 times theta minus 20. This gives 120 minus 1.5 theta = theta minus 20, so 140 = 2.5 theta. Therefore theta = 56 degrees C. The result lies between 20 degrees C and 80 degrees C as expected.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A quantity of gas occupies a certain volume when the temperature is -73oC and the pressure is 1.5 atmospheres. If the pressure is increased to 4.5 atmospheres and the volume is halved at the same time, what will be the new temperature of the gas?
questions.explanation: Use the combined gas law with absolute temperature: P1V1 divided by T1 equals P2V2 divided by T2. The initial temperature is minus 73 degrees C, which is 200 K. The pressure rises from 1.5 atm to 4.5 atm, so it triples, and the volume halves. Therefore T2 = 200 x 3 x 1 over 2 = 300 K, which is 27 degrees C. Hence option 4 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In a gas experiment, the pressure of the gas is plotted against the reciprocal of the volume of the gas at a constant temperature. the unit of the slope of the resulting curve is
questions.explanation: At constant temperature, Boyle’s law gives P proportional to 1 over V, so a graph of pressure against reciprocal of volume is a straight line with slope equal to PV.
