The unit of slope is pressure times volume, that is N m^-2 multiplied by m^3, which equals N m or joule. Joule is the unit of work or energy. Therefore option 2 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Water shows anomalous behaviour.
questions.explanation: Water behaves anomalously between 0 degrees C and 4 degrees C. In that interval, heating causes it to contract and cooling causes it to expand, opposite to the normal behaviour of most liquids. Its density is maximum at 4 degrees C, so the anomaly is not confined to just that single temperature. Therefore the correct interval is between 0 degrees C and 4 degrees C.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two thermo flasks of volume Vx and Vy are filled with liquid water at an initial temperature of 0oC. After sometime the temperature were found to be 9x, 9y, respectively. Given that \(\frac{Vx}{Vy}\) = 2 and \(\frac{\theta x}{\theta y}\) = \(\frac{1}{2}\) the ratio of the heat flow into the flask is
questions.explanation: Heat gained by each quantity of water is proportional to mass times specific heat times temperature rise. Both flasks contain water, so specific heat is the same, and mass is proportional to volume. Hence Qx divided by Qy equals Vx theta x divided by Vy theta y. Using Vx over Vy = 2 and theta x over theta y = 1 over 2 gives Qx over Qy = 1. Therefore the heat flow ratio is 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A good calorimeter should be of
options: low specific heat capacity and low heat conductivity
low specific heat capacity and high heat conductivity
high specific heat capacity and high heat conductivity
high specific heat capacity and low heat conductivity
dull surface and low heat conductivity
questions.explanation: A good calorimeter should take in as little heat as possible itself and should exchange minimal heat with the surroundings. That means the material should have low specific heat capacity, so little heat is required to raise its temperature, and low thermal conductivity, to reduce heat transfer through its walls. Hence the best description given is low specific heat capacity and low heat conductivity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements are NOT correct?
options: boiling occurs when the saturated vapour pressure of the liquid involved equals the external pressure
both the boiling point and the saturated vapour pressure of a given liquid depends on the external pressure
the saturated vapour presssure rises with increase in temperature
the saturated vapour pressure is independent of the volume available for the vapour
it is possible to boil water at a lower temperature than 100oC at high altitude
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs when a liquid’s saturated vapour pressure equals the external pressure, so option 0 is correct. Saturated vapour pressure for a given liquid depends only on temperature, not on the external pressure, though the boiling point does depend on external pressure. It also increases with temperature and is independent of vapour space volume. Water can therefore boil below 100 degrees C at high altitude. Option 1 is the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following phenomena CANNOT be explained by the molecular theory of matter?
questions.explanation: Molecular theory explains expansion, conduction in matter, convection in fluids, and evaporation through particle motion and interactions. Radiation is different because heat is transferred by electromagnetic waves and does not require a material medium or direct molecular contact. Therefore radiation is the listed phenomenon that cannot be explained solely by the molecular theory of matter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: In order to find the depth of the sea, a ship sends out a sound wave and receives an echo after one second. If the velocity of sound in water is 1500ms-1, what is the depth of the sea?
questions.explanation: The one second is the round trip time for the sound pulse to travel to the seabed and back. If the speed in water is 1500 m s^-1, the total distance travelled is 1500 m. The depth is half of this, so depth = 1500 divided by 2 = 750 m, which is 0.75 km. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When a sound wave passes from air into water its
options: speed and frequency increases but its wavelength remains the same
speed and wavelength increases but its frequency remains the same
speed remains the same but its frequency and wavelength change
speed increases but its frequency and wavelength decreases
questions.explanation: When a sound wave passes from air into water, its frequency remains unchanged because the source fixes the frequency. The speed changes because it depends on the medium, and sound travels faster in water than in air. Since speed equals frequency times wavelength, a higher speed with unchanged frequency means the wavelength increases. Therefore speed and wavelength increase while frequency remains the same.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe organ on a day when the speed of sound is 340ms-1 is 170Hz, then the length of the pipe is
questions.explanation: For a pipe closed at one end, the fundamental frequency is v divided by 4L. Rearranging gives L = v divided by 4f. Substituting v = 340 m s^-1 and f = 170 Hz gives L = 340 divided by 680 = 0.50 m. Converting to centimetres gives 50 cm. Therefore the pipe length is 50 cm.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An object is placed 15cm in front of a concave mirror of radius 40cm. The image formed
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, focal length equals half the radius, so f = 20 cm. The object is 15 cm from the mirror, which is inside the focal length, so the image must be virtual. Using the mirror formula with the usual sign convention gives 1 over 20 = 1 over 15 plus 1 over v, so 1 over v = minus 1 over 60 and v = minus 60 cm. Thus the image is 60 cm behind the mirror.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A 45o triangular glass prism can be used as a reflector of light because
options: A refraction never takes place in such a prism
the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence
the refractive index of glass is less than 1
the critival angle angle for glass is less than 45o
questions.explanation: A 45 degree prism can act as a reflector by total internal reflection. For total internal reflection to occur at the glass air boundary, the angle of incidence inside the glass must be greater than the critical angle. In this case the incidence is about 45 degrees, so reflection will occur only if the critical angle for glass is less than 45 degrees. Hence option 4 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A convex mirror is used as a driving mirror because i. its image is erect. ii. it has a large field of view. iii. it has a long focal length. Identify the CORRECT statement(s)
questions.explanation: A convex mirror forms images that are always virtual, erect, and diminished. The erect image is useful to a driver, and the mirror also gives a large field of view, allowing more of the road behind to be seen. Its use is not because it has a long focal length. Therefore the correct statements are i and ii only.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two rays of light from a point below the surface of water are equally inclined to each other at 60o in water. What is the angle between the rays when they emerge into air? (Take the refractive index of water to be \(\frac{4}{3}\))
questions.explanation: If the two rays are equally inclined and the angle between them in water is 60 degrees, each ray makes 30 degrees with the normal. By Snell’s law for water to air, 4 over 3 times sine 30 degrees equals sine r, so sine r = 2 over 3 and r is about 41.8 degrees. The emergent rays are symmetric, so the angle between them is 2r = 83.6 degrees.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A narrow beam of white light can be split up into different colours by a glass prism. The correct explanation is that
options: white light is an electromagnetic wave
the prism has all the colours of the white light
white light has undergone total internal reflection in the prism
different colours of white light travel with different speeds in glass
white ligth consist of yellow, green and red colours
questions.explanation: A prism disperses white light because different colours have different refractive indices in glass. Equivalently, the colours travel at different speeds in the glass and so are refracted by different amounts. This causes the beam to spread into its component colours. The effect is not due to total internal reflection and does not mean the prism already contains the colours. Therefore option 3 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A charge of one coulomb liberates 0.0033g of copper in an electrolytic process. How long will it take a current of 2A to librate 1.98g of copper in such a process?
questions.explanation: The mass deposited in electrolysis is proportional to the charge passed. If 1 C deposits 0.0033 g of copper, then depositing 1.98 g requires Q = 1.98 divided by 0.0033 = 600 C. With current I = 2 A, the time is t = Q divided by I = 600 divided by 2 = 300 s. That is 5 minutes. Therefore option 0 is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If the distance between two stationary charged particle is doubled, the magnitude of the electro-static force between them will be
options: a quarter of its former value
questions.explanation: Coulomb’s law states that the electrostatic force between two point charges varies inversely as the square of their separation. If the distance is doubled, the new force becomes 1 divided by 2 squared of the original value, which is 1 over 4. Therefore the force becomes a quarter of its former value. The sign of the force may differ, but its magnitude is reduced to one quarter.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following methods CANNOT be used to produce a steel magnet? The
options: passing of an electric current through a solenoid
repeated stroking of the specimen with a magnet
repeated stroking of the specimen in opposite directions with magnets
hammering of the specimen in the earth's magnetic field
questions.explanation: Steel can be magnetized by stroking, by placing it in a solenoid carrying current, or by hammering it in Earth’s magnetic field. Heating does not produce magnetization; instead it tends to randomize magnetic domains and weaken or destroy existing magnetism, especially near the Curie temperature. Therefore the method that cannot be used to produce a steel magnet is heating of the specimen.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A cell gives a current of 0.15A through a resistance of 8\(\Omega\) and 0.3A. When the resistance is changed to 3\(\Omega\) the internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation: Let the emf be E and internal resistance be r. For a cell delivering current I through external resistance R, E = I(R + r). First case: E = 0.15(8 + r). Second case: E = 0.30(3 + r). Equating gives 0.15(8 + r) = 0.30(3 + r), so 1.2 + 0.15r = 0.9 + 0.30r, hence 0.3 = 0.15r and r = 2.0 ohms. That matches option index 3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following will convert a milliammeter to a voltmeter?
options: parallel resistance equal to milliammeter resistance
questions.explanation: A voltmeter must draw very little current, so it must have a high total resistance. To convert a milliammeter into a voltmeter, a large resistance is connected in series with it so that the current through the meter remains small while the instrument responds to potential difference. A parallel resistance would instead be used in ammeter conversion. Therefore high series resistance is correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A wire P has half the diameter and half the length of a wire Q of similar material. The ratio of the resistance of P to that of Q is
questions.explanation: Resistance is proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross sectional area. For similar materials, R = rho L over A and area is proportional to diameter squared. Wire P has half the length of Q and half the diameter, so its area is one quarter of Q’s. Therefore Rp over Rq = one half divided by one quarter = 2. The ratio is 2 to 1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: An electric kettle, connected to a 240V mains, produces 6.0 x 105J of heat energy to boil a quantity of water in 5 minutes. Find the resistance of the kettle.
questions.explanation: Electrical energy supplied by a resistor is E = V squared t over R. Rearranging gives R = V squared t divided by E. With V = 240 V, t = 5 minutes = 300 s, and E = 6.0 x 10^5 J, R = 240 squared x 300 divided by 6.0 x 10^5 = 28.8 ohms. The unit is ohm, as required for resistance.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: On which of the following does the operation of a moving coil ammeter depend? i. Electromagnetic induction ii. Force on a carrying-current conductor iii. Magnetic effect of an electric current
questions.explanation: A moving coil ammeter operates because a current carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque. That directly involves the force on a current carrying conductor and also the magnetic effect of electric current. Electromagnetic induction is not the operating principle here because no induced emf from changing flux is required for the instrument to function. Therefore ii and iii only are correct.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A galvanometer can be converted to an ammeter with a different range by connecting a high resistance in series
An electric current always produces a magnetic field
Maxwell's screw rule states that if a corkscrew moves inthe direction of the current, the hand turns in the direction of the lines of force
Electromagnets are used in electric bells and telephone recievers
The lines of force round a straight current carrying conductor are circular
questions.explanation: A galvanometer is converted to an ammeter by connecting a low resistance shunt in parallel, not a high resistance in series. A high series resistance is used to convert it into a voltmeter. The other statements are standard: currents produce magnetic fields, Maxwell’s screw rule gives field direction, electromagnets are used in bells and receivers, and field lines around a straight conductor are circular. Hence option 0 is the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A transformer has a primary coil with 500 turns and a secondary coil with 2500 turns. When the voltage input to the primary coil is 120V, the output is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, output voltage divided by input voltage equals secondary turns divided by primary turns. Thus Vs over 120 = 2500 over 500 = 5. Therefore Vs = 120 x 5 = 600 V. The transformer is step up because the secondary has more turns than the primary. Hence the correct output is 600 V.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements about electrolysis is NOT correct?
options: The substances in solution in the electrolyte become ionized
Ions are electrically charged and are attracted towards electrodes when a potential difference is applied
Ions may be discharged at the electrodes, forming bubbles or deposits
The mass deposited depends upon the length of time for which current flows
The mass of gas set free or metal deposited is proportional to the square of the current
questions.explanation: Faraday’s first law states that the mass deposited is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed, that is current multiplied by time. Therefore the deposited mass is proportional to current for fixed time, not to the square of the current. The other statements correctly describe ionization, motion of ions, discharge at electrodes, and dependence on duration of current flow. Hence option 4 is the incorrect statement.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: The average range of distinct vision for a normal eye is from the far distance (infinity) up to about 25cm in front of the eye
Longsighted people have difficulty in making the eye lense sufficiently powerful to focus on nearby objects
Shortsighted people cannot accommodate distant objects
Longsighted people need diverging spectacle lenses
A person with long sight has his eye-ball too short and the image of an object is therefore formed behind the retina
questions.explanation: Long sight, or hypermetropia, is corrected with a converging lens, not a diverging lens. A long sighted person has difficulty focusing on near objects because the eye cannot make the lens sufficiently powerful, often associated with an eyeball that is effectively too short so the image would form behind the retina. Therefore the incorrect statement is that longsighted people need diverging spectacle lenses.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What is the number of neutrons in the Uranium isotope \(^{238}_{92}X\)?
questions.explanation: In nuclear physics, the number of neutrons in a nuclide is determined by subtracting the atomic number (Z, the number of protons) from the mass number (A, total nucleons): N = A - Z. Applying this standard relationship to the given isotope gives 146. Thus, 146 represents the exact number of neutrons.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: For which of the underlisted quantities is the derived unit \(ML^2T^{-2}\) correct? i. moment of a force ii. work iii. acceleration
questions.explanation: In dimensional analysis, physical quantities are expressed in terms of fundamental dimensions: mass [M], length [L], and time [T]. Deriving the dimensions from the defining physical formula and base SI units confirms that i and ii correctly matches the dimensional representation of the quantity.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: What volume of alcohol with a density of 8.4 x 102kgm-3 will have the same mass as 4.2m3of petrol whose density is 7.2 x 102kgm-3?
questions.explanation: According to Archimedes’ principle, a body fully or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force (upthrust) equal to the weight of fluid displaced: U = Vρg. Relative density is defined as the density of substance divided by the density of water (or weight in air over loss of weight in water). Solving the mass and volume relations gives 3.6m3.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: For correcting long sight defects in the human eye we require a
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, converging lens is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that converging lens is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: For a concave mirror to form a teal diminished image, the object must be placed
options: between the mirror and its focus
between the focus and the centre of curvature
at a distance greater than the radius of curvature
questions.explanation: Image formation in thin lenses and spherical mirrors follows the fundamental mirror and lens formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v (with standard Cartesian sign convention), and linear magnification is m = |v/u| = image size / object size. Substituting the object distance and focal length yields at a distance greater than the radius of curvature.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The unit of quantity of electricity is called
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, the coulomb is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that the coulomb is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The resistance of a wire depends on
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, all of the above is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that all of the above is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Two cells each of e.m.f. 1.5V and an internal resistance 2\(\Omega\) are connected in parallel. Calculate the current flowing when the cells are connected to a 1\(\Omega\) resistor
questions.explanation: For an electric cell or battery of electromotive force E and internal resistance r connected across an external circuit, the terminal potential difference is given by V = E - Ir = IR. Using Ohm’s law I = E / (R + r) and substituting the stated circuit parameters yields 0.75Ω. Therefore, 0.75Ω is the correct result.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following components is NOT contained in a dry cell? A
questions.explanation: From established physical laws and empirical principles in physics, copper rod accurately characterizes the system under consideration. The competing alternatives either misstate the physical relationship or violate standard conservation and thermodynamic laws. Therefore, copper rod is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following can be described as high tension transmission?
questions.explanation: From established physical laws and empirical principles in physics, low current and high voltage accurately characterizes the system under consideration. The competing alternatives either misstate the physical relationship or violate standard conservation and thermodynamic laws. Therefore, low current and high voltage is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: All the heat generated in a 5\(\Omega\) resistor by 2A flowing for 30 seconds is used to evaporate 5g of a liquid at its boiling point. Which of the following is the correct value of the specific latent heat of the liquid?
questions.explanation: Thermal energy absorbed or released during a temperature change is given by Q = mcΔθ (where m is mass, c is specific heat capacity, and Δθ is temperature change), and during phase change without temperature variation by Q = mL (where L is specific latent heat). Equating heat gained to heat lost yields 120Jg-1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: When vibration occurs in air column, the distance between a node and an antinode is equal to
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, one-quarter of the wavelength is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that one-quarter of the wavelength is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements is (are) NOT correct? i. pressure changes do not affect the speed of sound in air ii. the velocity of sound increases with temperature iii. the quality of the note depends only on its frequency
questions.explanation: The fundamental wave relationship connecting propagation velocity v, frequency f, and wavelength λ is v = fλ (or T = 1/f). For sound and electromagnetic waves traveling through a uniform medium, wave speed is constant, meaning wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency. Calculating with the given parameters produces i and iii.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: One of two identical tuning forks with natural frequency 256Hz, one is loaded so that 4 beats per second are heard when they are sounded together. What is the frequency of the loaded tuning fork?
questions.explanation: The fundamental wave relationship connecting propagation velocity v, frequency f, and wavelength λ is v = fλ (or T = 1/f). For sound and electromagnetic waves traveling through a uniform medium, wave speed is constant, meaning wavelength is inversely proportional to frequency. Calculating with the given parameters produces 252Hz.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Dewpoint is the temperature at which, water vapour in the atmosphere
options: is just sufficient to cause cooling
has a relative humidity of fifty percent
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, first condenses into liquid form is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that first condenses into liquid form is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: The lower and upper fixed points marked on a mecury-in-glass thermometer are 210mm apart. The end of the mercury column in the tube is 49mm above the lower fixed point in a room. What is the temperature of the room in degrees Celsius?
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, 23.3oC is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that 23.3oC is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: If a solid changes directly into a gas when heat is applied the process is called
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, sublimation is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that sublimation is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A plane inclined at an angle of 30o to the horizontal has an efficiency of 60%. The force parallel to the plane required to push a load of 120N uniformly up the plane is
questions.explanation: For any simple machine, Mechanical Advantage is MA = Load / Effort, Velocity Ratio is VR = distance moved by effort / distance moved by load, and Efficiency is η = (MA / VR) × 100%. Substituting the given load, effort, and velocity ratio into these definitions leads directly to 100N.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A body of mass 5kg initially at rest is acted upon by two mutually perpendicular forces 12N and 5N as shown in fig.3. If the particle moves in the direction QA, calculate the magnitude of the acceleration
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, 2.60ms-2 is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that 2.60ms-2 is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A small steel needle is carefully floated on water in a beaker. When a few drops of kerosine are introduced into the water the needle sink. Which of the following statements correctly explain(s) the observation? i. there is tension on the water surface ii. kerosine reduces the density of water so that needle becomes denser than water iii. kerosine reduces the surface tension of water
questions.explanation: According to Archimedes’ principle, a body fully or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force (upthrust) equal to the weight of fluid displaced: U = Vρg. Relative density is defined as the density of substance divided by the density of water (or weight in air over loss of weight in water). Solving the mass and volume relations gives i and iii.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Which of the following statements describes an atom accurately? i. atoms of all elements are identical ii. an atom contains a nucleus and number of electrons iii. due to the electrons in the atom an atom is negatively charged iv. electrons in the atom move in circular orbits round the nucleus
questions.explanation: From established physical laws and empirical principles in physics, ii and iv only accurately characterizes the system under consideration. The competing alternatives either misstate the physical relationship or violate standard conservation and thermodynamic laws. Therefore, ii and iv only is the correct answer.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A particle moves in a circular orbit of radius 0.02m. If the speed of the particle is 0.88ms-1, calculate its frequency in cycles per second
questions.explanation: According to fundamental physics principles, 7.0Hz is the verified result. Evaluating the governing physical laws, equations, and boundary conditions presented in the question decisively confirms that 7.0Hz is the appropriate option.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: Heat is supplied uniformly at the rate of 100W to 1.0 x 10-2kg of a liquid for 20 seconds. If the temperature of the liquid rises by 5oC, then the specific heat capacity of the liquid is
questions.explanation: Thermal energy absorbed or released during a temperature change is given by Q = mcΔθ (where m is mass, c is specific heat capacity, and Δθ is temperature change), and during phase change without temperature variation by Q = mL (where L is specific latent heat). Equating heat gained to heat lost yields 4.0 x 104Jkg-1k-1.

questions.subject: physics
questions.text: A given mass of an ideal gas occupies a volume V at a temperature T and under a pressure p. If the pressure is increased to 2p and the temperature reduced to \(\frac{1}{2T}\), then the percentage change in the volume of the gas is
